# Page: Overview

# Overview

This document provides a comprehensive technical overview of the Reseek codebase, a high-performance protein structure search and alignment tool. Reseek implements a novel sequence alignment algorithm using a "mega-alphabet" of ~10^11 distinct states to achieve improved sensitivity over existing methods like DALI, TM-align, and Foldseek.

For detailed information about specific subsystems, see the related wiki pages: [Getting Started](#2) covers installation and basic usage, [Core Alignment Engine](#3) documents the central algorithms, [Database Search System](#4) covers multi-threaded search architecture, and [Command-Line Interface](#6) provides complete reference documentation.

## System Architecture

Reseek is organized as a modular C++ application with five primary architectural layers:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Command Interface Layer"
        CLI["`reseek_main.cpp`<br/>Main Entry Point"]
        OPTS["`myopts.h`<br/>217+ Configuration Parameters"]
        CMDS["`cmds.h`<br/>69 Commands"]
        USAGE["`usage.h`<br/>Help System"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Processing Layer"
        ALIGNER["`DSSAligner`<br/>Central Alignment Engine"]
        PARAMS["`DSSParams`<br/>Algorithm Configuration"]
        SEARCH["`DBSearcher`<br/>Database Search Orchestrator"]
        LOADER["`ProfileLoader`<br/>Multi-threaded Chain Loading"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Processing Layer"
        CONVERT["`cmd_convert`<br/>Format Conversion"]
        READER["`ChainReader2`<br/>Universal Format Parser"]
        FILTER["`MuFilter + PostMuFilter`<br/>Two-Stage Filtering"]
        CHAIN["`PDBChain`<br/>Structure Representation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Layer"
        FIELDS["`UserField System`<br/>Configurable Output Columns"]
        FORMATS["`Multiple Output Formats`<br/>TSV, FASTA, Alignments"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis Layer"
        BENCH["`SCOP40Bench`<br/>Performance Benchmarking"]
        CALIB["`Calibration System`<br/>Statistical Model Tuning"]
    end
    
    CLI --> OPTS
    CLI --> CMDS
    CLI --> USAGE
    CLI --> ALIGNER
    CLI --> SEARCH
    CLI --> CONVERT
    CLI --> BENCH
    
    ALIGNER --> PARAMS
    SEARCH --> LOADER
    SEARCH --> FILTER
    CONVERT --> READER
    READER --> CHAIN
    FILTER --> ALIGNER
    ALIGNER --> FIELDS
    FIELDS --> FORMATS
    BENCH --> CALIB
    
    style CLI fill:#f9f9f9
    style ALIGNER fill:#f9f9f9
    style SEARCH fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [src/reseek_main.cpp](), [src/myopts.h:1-150](), [src/cmds.h:1-79](), [src/usage.h:1-90]()

## Core Components

### Command System and Configuration

The application uses a sophisticated command and parameter system centered around three key files:

| Component | Purpose | Scale |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| `myopts.h` | Parameter definitions | 217+ parameters across STR_OPT, UNS_OPT, FLT_OPT, FLAG_OPT types |
| `cmds.h` | Command definitions | 69 commands including search, convert, alignpair, benchmarking |
| `usage.h` | Help system | Comprehensive usage documentation |

The parameter system supports string options (`STR_OPT`), unsigned integer options (`UNS_OPT`), floating-point options (`FLT_OPT`), and boolean flags (`FLAG_OPT`).

Sources: [src/myopts.h:1-150](), [src/cmds.h:1-79](), [src/usage.h:1-90]()

### Data Processing Pipeline

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input Formats"
        PDB["`PDB Files`<br/>Legacy Format"]
        CIF["`CIF/mmCIF Files`<br/>Modern Standard"]
        CAL["`CAL Files`<br/>C-alpha Coordinates"]
        BCA["`BCA Files`<br/>Binary C-alpha"]
        FASTA["`FASTA Files`<br/>Sequence Data"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing Core"
        READER2["`ChainReader2`<br/>Universal Parser"]
        CHAIN2["`PDBChain`<br/>Unified Representation"]
        SEQDB["`SeqDB`<br/>Sequence Management"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Search Pipeline"
        MUKMER["`MuKmerFilter`<br/>K-mer Pre-screening"]
        MUFILTER["`MuFilter`<br/>Fast Initial Filter"]
        POSTMU["`PostMuFilter`<br/>Detailed Alignment"]
        DSSALN["`DSSAligner`<br/>Core Alignment Engine"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Generation"
        USERFIELDS["`UserField System`<br/>Configurable Columns"]
        OUTPUTS["`Multiple Formats`<br/>TSV, FASTA, Alignments"]
    end
    
    PDB --> READER2
    CIF --> READER2
    CAL --> READER2
    BCA --> READER2
    FASTA --> READER2
    
    READER2 --> CHAIN2
    READER2 --> SEQDB
    
    CHAIN2 --> MUKMER
    MUKMER --> MUFILTER
    MUFILTER --> POSTMU
    POSTMU --> DSSALN
    
    DSSALN --> USERFIELDS
    USERFIELDS --> OUTPUTS
```

The pipeline implements a multi-stage filtering approach to balance speed and sensitivity, with each stage progressively more computationally intensive but more selective.

Sources: [src/chainreader2.h](), [src/pdbchain.h](), [src/seqdb.h](), [src/mukmerfilter.h](), [src/postmufilter.cpp](), [src/dssaligner.h]()

### Algorithm Modes and Configuration

Reseek provides three primary algorithm modes controlled by the `DSSParams` configuration system:

| Mode | Purpose | Performance Trade-off |
|------|---------|----------------------|
| `--fast` | High-speed searches | Optimized for speed, moderate sensitivity |
| `--sensitive` | Balanced performance | Default mode balancing speed and sensitivity |
| `--verysensitive` | Maximum sensitivity | Comprehensive search, slower execution |

The `DSSParams` class centralizes algorithm configuration, managing feature weights, gap penalties, score matrices, and statistical models.

Sources: [src/dssparams.h](), [src/dssparams.cpp]()

### Output System

The flexible output system uses the `UserField` enumeration to provide configurable column selection:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Core Output Fields"
        QUERY["`UF_query`<br/>Query identifier"]
        TARGET["`UF_target`<br/>Target identifier"]
        COORDS["`UF_qlo, UF_qhi, UF_tlo, UF_thi`<br/>Alignment coordinates"]
        STATS["`UF_evalue, UF_pvalue`<br/>Statistical significance"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Alignment Details"
        IDENTITY["`UF_pctid`<br/>Percent identity"]
        CIGAR["`UF_cigar`<br/>CIGAR string"]
        ROWS["`UF_qrow, UF_trow`<br/>Aligned sequences"]
        QUALITY["`UF_aq`<br/>Alignment quality score"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Advanced Metrics"
        LDDT["`UF_lddt`<br/>Local Distance Difference Test"]
        SCORES["`UF_raw, UF_dpscore`<br/>Raw alignment scores"]
        GAPS["`UF_gaps, UF_ids`<br/>Gap and identity counts"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Generation"
        WRITER["`DSSAligner::WriteUserField`<br/>Field formatting and output"]
    end
    
    QUERY --> WRITER
    TARGET --> WRITER
    COORDS --> WRITER
    STATS --> WRITER
    IDENTITY --> WRITER
    CIGAR --> WRITER
    ROWS --> WRITER
    QUALITY --> WRITER
    LDDT --> WRITER
    SCORES --> WRITER
    GAPS --> WRITER
```

Default output includes `aq+query+target+evalue+pvalue`, with standard output (`std`) providing `query+target+qlo+qhi+ql+tlo+thi+tl+pctid+evalue`.

Sources: [src/userfields.cpp:1-152](), [src/userfieldnames.h:1-34]()

## Build System and Platform Support

Reseek supports cross-platform compilation with dedicated build configurations:

| Platform | Build Method | Configuration |
|----------|--------------|---------------|
| Linux x86 | `build_linux_x86.bash` | GCC with OpenMP |
| macOS x86 | `build_osx_x86.bash` | Clang with OpenMP |
| Windows | Visual Studio | `reseek.vcxproj` with MSVC |

The Visual Studio project file defines comprehensive build configurations with optimization settings, OpenMP support, and multi-processor compilation enabled.

Sources: [src/reseek.vcxproj:1-564](), [src/reseek.vcxproj.filters:1-874]()

## Performance and Benchmarking

The codebase includes extensive benchmarking infrastructure centered around the SCOP40 benchmark:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Benchmarking Infrastructure"
        SCOP40["`SCOP40Bench`<br/>Gold Standard Evaluation"]
        ROC["`ROC Analysis`<br/>Sensitivity/Specificity"]
        CALIB["`Calibration System`<br/>Statistical Model Fitting"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Performance Metrics"
        SENS["`Sensitivity`<br/>True Positive Rate"]
        SPEC["`Specificity`<br/>True Negative Rate"]

    end
    
    subgraph "Quality Outputs"

    end
    
    SCOP40 --> SENS
    SCOP40 --> SPEC
    ROC --> CURVES
    CALIB --> EVAL
    CALIB --> MODELS
    SENS --> REPORTS
    SPEC --> REPORTS
    EVAL --> REPORTS
```

The benchmarking system measures performance against the SCOP40 superfamily classification, focusing on the regime with false-positive rates <10 per query.

Sources: [src/scop40bench.h](), [src/scop40bench.cpp](), [src/scop40benchroc.cpp]()

## Threading and Memory Management

Reseek implements multi-threaded processing with custom memory management:

- **Threading**: OpenMP-based parallelization controlled by `--threads` parameter
- **Memory**: Custom allocators in `mymalloc.cpp` with platform-specific implementations
- **Database Loading**: `ProfileLoader` class manages multi-threaded chain loading
- **Search**: `DBSearcher` orchestrates parallel database searches

The threading model scales automatically to available CPU cores while providing manual control for performance tuning.

Sources: [src/profileloader.h](), [src/dbsearcher.h](), [src/mymalloc.cpp](), [src/runthreads.cpp]()

# Page: Getting Started

# Getting Started

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

This document provides installation instructions, build procedures, and basic usage examples for the reseek protein structure search and alignment tool. It covers the essential steps needed to compile, install, and run reseek for common use cases including database searches, pairwise alignments, and format conversions.

For detailed information about the core alignment algorithms, see [Core Alignment Engine](#3). For comprehensive command-line reference, see [Command-Line Interface](#6). For data format specifications, see [Data Processing and Formats](#5).

## Installation and Build Process

Reseek supports compilation on Linux, macOS, and Windows platforms. The build system uses platform-specific bash scripts that handle dependency resolution and linking.

### Build Requirements

The build process requires:
- C++ compiler with C++11 support
- Standard development tools (make, shell)
- For automated builds: Python 3.10+ and platform-specific package managers

### Linux x86_64 Build

```bash
cd src/
chmod +x build_linux_x86.bash
./build_linux_x86.bash
```

The build script creates a static binary at `bin/reseek`. Static linking warnings about `dlopen` are expected and safe to ignore [README.md:108-112]().

### macOS x86_64 Build

```bash
cd src/
chmod +x build_osx_x86.bash
./build_osx_x86.bash
```

The macOS build requires GCC 11 and uses MacPorts for dependency management.

### Windows Build

Load `reseek.vcxproj` into Microsoft Visual Studio and use the Build command [README.md:105]().

### Build Artifacts

The build process generates these key files:
- `bin/reseek` - Main executable
- `Makefile` - Generated build configuration
- `gitver.txt` - Version information

**Build Process Flow**

```mermaid
    end
```

## Basic Usage Workflow

Reseek operates through three primary commands that handle different alignment scenarios. Each command requires specific algorithm sensitivity settings.

### Core Commands and Algorithm Modes

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Main Commands"
        SEARCH["cmd_search"]
        CONVERT["cmd_convert"]
        ALIGNPAIR["cmd_alignpair"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Algorithm Modes"
        FAST["-fast"]
        SENSITIVE["-sensitive"]
        VERYSENSITIVE["-verysensitive"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        CHAINREADER["ChainReader2"]
        PDBCHAIN["PDBChain"]
        SEQDB["SeqDB"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Generation"
        USERFIELD["UserField system"]
        WRITEOUTPUT["DSSAligner::WriteUserField"]
    end
    
    SEARCH --> FAST
    SEARCH --> SENSITIVE
    SEARCH --> VERYSENSITIVE
    
    SEARCH --> CHAINREADER
    ALIGNPAIR --> CHAINREADER
    CONVERT --> CHAINREADER
    
    CHAINREADER --> PDBCHAIN
    PDBCHAIN --> SEQDB
    
    SEARCH --> USERFIELD
    ALIGNPAIR --> USERFIELD
    USERFIELD --> WRITEOUTPUT
```

Sources: [README.md:15-34](), [src/usage.h:4-11](), [src/userfields.cpp:45-151]()

### Database Search Example

```bash
# Create binary database (recommended for large datasets)
reseek -convert /data/PDB_mirror/ -bca PDB.bca

# Search against database
reseek -search query.pdb -db PDB.bca -sensitive -output hits.txt
```

### Pairwise Alignment Example

```bash
# Align and superpose two structures
reseek -alignpair 1XYZ.pdb -input2 2ABC.pdb -sensitive \
       -aln alignment.txt -output superposed.pdb
```

### All-vs-All Search Example

```bash
# Compare all structures against each other
reseek -search structures/ -fast -output all_hits.txt
```

## File Format Support

Reseek supports multiple input and output formats optimized for different use cases. The format conversion system handles automatic detection and conversion between formats.

### Input Formats

| Format | Extension | Description | Use Case |
|--------|-----------|-------------|----------|
| PDB | `.pdb` | Legacy PDB format | Individual structures |
| mmCIF | `.cif`, `.mmcif` | Modern PDBx/mmCIF format | Large structures, NMR |
| CAL | `.cal` | C-alpha coordinates (text) | Reduced representation |
| BCA | `.bca` | Binary C-alpha format | Large databases |
| FASTA | `.fasta` | Amino acid sequences | Sequence-only analysis |
| Files List | `.files` | List of structure files | Batch processing |

### Format Conversion

```bash
# Convert PDB files to binary database
reseek -convert input_dir/ -bca output.bca

# Convert to multiple formats
reseek -convert structures.pdb -cal output.cal -fasta output.fasta
```

**Format Processing Pipeline**

```mermaid

    end
    
    subgraph "Processing Layer"

        PDBCHAIN["PDBChain"]
    end

    end

    end

    COORDS --> OUTBCA
    SEQUENCE --> OUTFASTA
```

Sources: [README.md:70-87](), [src/usage.h:60-81]()

## Output Configuration

Reseek provides extensive output customization through the UserField system. Users can specify exactly which columns to include in results using the `-columns` parameter.

### Standard Output Columns

The UserField system defines these output options [src/userfieldnames.h:5-32]():

| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| `query` | Query structure label | `1ABC_A` |
| `target` | Target structure label | `2XYZ_B` |
| `evalue` | E-value statistical significance | `1.2e-5` |
| `pvalue` | P-value statistical significance | `3.4e-6` |
| `qlo`, `qhi` | Query alignment bounds | `15`, `127` |
| `tlo`, `thi` | Target alignment bounds | `8`, `119` |
| `ql`, `tl` | Query/target sequence lengths | `150`, `142` |
| `pctid` | Percent identity | `34.5` |
| `aq` | Alignment quality (0-1) | `0.742` |
| `cigar` | CIGAR alignment string | `25M3D47M` |

### Custom Output Examples

```bash
# Default output (AQ + labels + statistics)
reseek -search query.pdb -db target.bca -sensitive -output hits.txt

# Custom columns
reseek -search query.pdb -db target.bca -sensitive \
       -columns "query+target+evalue+pctid+aq" -output custom.txt

# Standard format with all basic fields
reseek -search query.pdb -db target.bca -sensitive \
       -columns "std" -output standard.txt
```

```mermaid
    ALIGNMENT_DATA --> STATISTICS
    STATISTICS --> WRITEUF

    WRITEUF --> FORMATTING

```

Sources: [src/userfields.cpp:6-151](), [src/userfieldnames.h:1-34](), [README.md:36-59](), [src/usage.h:25-48]()

## Common Parameters

### Required Algorithm Mode

Every alignment command requires one of these sensitivity modes:
- `-fast`: Fastest execution, lower sensitivity
- `-sensitive`: Balanced speed and sensitivity  
- `-verysensitive`: Highest sensitivity, slower execution

### Optional Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `-evalue E` | Maximum E-value threshold | `10` (except `-verysensitive`) |
| `-pvalue P` | Minimum P-value threshold | `1` |
| `-threads N` | Number of parallel threads | Number of CPU cores |
| `-gapopen X` | Gap opening penalty | Algorithm-dependent |
| `-gapext X` | Gap extension penalty | Algorithm-dependent |
| `-log FILE` | Log file for errors and timing | None |

### Example with Parameters

```bash
reseek -search query.pdb -db large_db.bca -sensitive \
       -evalue 0.01 -threads 8 -log search.log \
       -columns "query+target+evalue+aq+pctid" \
       -output results.txt
```

Sources: [README.md:61-69](), [src/usage.h:50-85]()

# Page: Core Alignment Engine

# Core Alignment Engine

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/dssaligner.cpp](src/dssaligner.cpp)
- [src/dssaligner.h](src/dssaligner.h)
- [src/dssparams.cpp](src/dssparams.cpp)
- [src/dssparams.h](src/dssparams.h)
- [src/namedparams.cpp](src/namedparams.cpp)

</details>



The Core Alignment Engine is the computational heart of the reseek protein structure search system. It performs pairwise sequence and structural alignments between query and target protein chains using a sophisticated multi-feature scoring system combined with dynamic programming algorithms. This engine handles the computationally intensive task of finding optimal alignments and calculating statistical significance values.

For database search orchestration and multi-threading, see [Database Search System](#4). For input/output format handling, see [Data Processing and Formats](#5). For parameter configuration details, see [Parameter Configuration](#3.2).

## Architecture Overview

The alignment engine centers around the `DSSAligner` class, which coordinates multiple alignment algorithms, scoring systems, and performance optimizations.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Core Classes"

        DSSParams["DSSParams<br/>Configuration & scoring"]
        XDPMem["XDPMem<br/>Dynamic programming memory"]
        MuKmerFilter["MuKmerFilter<br/>K-mer pre-filtering"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input Data"
        PDBChainA["PDBChain A<br/>Query structure"]
        PDBChainB["PDBChain B<br/>Target structure"]
        ProfileA["Profile A<br/>Feature vectors"]
        ProfileB["Profile B<br/>Feature vectors"]
        MuLettersA["MuLetters A<br/>Reduced alphabet"]
        MuLettersB["MuLetters B<br/>Reduced alphabet"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Alignment Algorithms"
        SWFast["SWFast<br/>Smith-Waterman DP"]
        AlignMKF["AlignMKF<br/>K-mer filtered alignment"]
        AlignMuQP["AlignMuQP<br/>Quick profile alignment"]
        XDropHSP["XDropHSP<br/>Extension algorithm"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Scoring Components"

    subgraph "Output"

    end
    
    DSSAligner --> DSSParams

    PDBChainB --> DSSAligner
    ProfileA --> DSSAligner
    ProfileB --> DSSAligner

    MuLettersB --> DSSAligner
    
    DSSAligner --> SWFast
    DSSAligner --> AlignMKF
    DSSAligner --> AlignMuQP
    DSSAligner --> XDropHSP
    
    DSSParams --> ScoreMxs
    DSSAligner --> SetSMx_NoRev
    DSSAligner --> GetScorePosPair

    CalcEvalue --> LDDT
```

Sources: [src/dssaligner.h:18-231](), [src/dssaligner.cpp:92-103](), [src/dssparams.h:27-118]()

## Core Alignment Workflow

The alignment process follows a multi-stage pipeline with progressive filtering and refinement stages.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        SetQuery["SetQuery()<br/>Configure query chain"]
        SetTarget["SetTarget()<br/>Configure target chain"]
        SetParams["SetParams()<br/>Load configuration"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Pre-filtering Stage"
        DoMKF["DoMKF()<br/>Check k-mer filter eligibility"]
        MuFilter["MuFilter()<br/>Quick sequence filter"]
        MKFAlign["AlignMKF()<br/>K-mer guided alignment"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Similarity Matrix Stage"
        SetSMx["SetSMx_NoRev()<br/>Build similarity matrix"]
        SetMuQP["SetMuQP()<br/>Build Mu profiles"]
        AllocSMxData["AllocSMxData()<br/>Allocate matrix memory"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Dynamic Programming Stage"
        SWFast["SWFast()<br/>Smith-Waterman alignment"]
        GetPath["m_Path<br/>Store alignment path"]
        GetScore["m_AlnFwdScore<br/>Store alignment score"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Post-processing Stage"
        GetPathCounts["GetPathCounts()<br/>Count M/D/I operations"]
        GetLDDT["GetLDDT()<br/>Calculate structural similarity"]
        CalcEvalue["CalcEvalue()<br/>Calculate statistical significance"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Stage"
        ToTsv["ToTsv()<br/>Tabular output"]
        ToFasta2["ToFasta2()<br/>Alignment output"]
        ToAln["ToAln()<br/>Pretty alignment"]
    end
    
    SetQuery --> SetTarget
    SetTarget --> SetParams
    SetParams --> DoMKF
    
    DoMKF -->|"Large sequences"| MKFAlign
    DoMKF -->|"Small sequences"| MuFilter
    MKFAlign --> GetPath
    
    MuFilter -->|"Pass filter"| SetSMx
    MuFilter -->|"Fail filter"| Output[Return early]
    
    SetSMx --> SetMuQP
    SetMuQP --> AllocSMxData
    AllocSMxData --> SWFast
    
    SWFast --> GetPath
    SWFast --> GetScore
    GetScore --> GetPathCounts
    GetPathCounts --> GetLDDT
    GetLDDT --> CalcEvalue
    
    CalcEvalue --> ToTsv
    CalcEvalue --> ToFasta2
    CalcEvalue --> ToAln
```

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:783-821](), [src/dssaligner.cpp:923-939](), [src/dssaligner.cpp:1358-1403]()

## DSSAligner Class Structure

The `DSSAligner` class maintains alignment state and provides the main interface for performing alignments.

### Key Member Variables

| Variable | Type | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| `m_ChainA`, `m_ChainB` | `const PDBChain*` | Input protein chains |
| `m_ProfileA`, `m_ProfileB` | `const vector<vector<byte>>*` | Multi-feature profiles |
| `m_MuLettersA`, `m_MuLettersB` | `const vector<byte>*` | Reduced alphabet sequences |
| `m_Path` | `string` | Alignment path (M/D/I operations) |
| `m_LoA`, `m_LoB` | `uint` | Alignment start positions |
| `m_HiA`, `m_HiB` | `uint` | Alignment end positions |
| `m_EvalueA`, `m_EvalueB` | `float` | Statistical significance values |
| `m_AlnFwdScore` | `float` | Forward alignment score |
| `m_SMx_Data` | `float**` | Similarity matrix data |

### Core Alignment Methods

#### Primary Alignment Interface
- `AlignQueryTarget()` - Main alignment entry point [src/dssaligner.cpp:783-821]()
- `SetQuery()` - Configure query sequence and features [src/dssaligner.cpp:664-689]()
- `SetTarget()` - Configure target sequence and features [src/dssaligner.cpp:691-703]()

#### Specialized Alignment Algorithms
- `Align_NoAccel()` - Standard Smith-Waterman alignment [src/dssaligner.cpp:923-939]()
- `AlignMKF()` - K-mer filtered alignment for large sequences [src/dssaligner.cpp:1358-1363]()
- `AlignMuQP()` - Quick profile alignment with reduced alphabet [src/dssaligner.cpp:1041-1061]()

#### Scoring and Evaluation
- `GetScorePosPair()` - Calculate score for aligned position pair [src/dssaligner.cpp:320-347]()
- `CalcEvalue()` - Calculate statistical significance using LDDT and other features [src/dssaligner.cpp:844-898]()
- `GetLDDT()` - Calculate local distance difference test score [src/dssaligner.cpp:1283-1294]()

Sources: [src/dssaligner.h:18-231](), [src/dssaligner.cpp:100-139]()

## Multi-Feature Scoring System

The alignment engine uses a sophisticated multi-feature scoring system that combines sequence and structural information.

### Feature Integration Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Feature Types"
        AA["FEATURE_AA<br/>Amino acid identity"]
        NENDist["FEATURE_NENDist<br/>N-terminal distance"]
        Conf["FEATURE_Conf<br/>Confidence scores"]
        NENConf["FEATURE_NENConf<br/>N-terminal confidence"]
        RENDist["FEATURE_RENDist<br/>Relative distance"]
        DstNxtHlx["FEATURE_DstNxtHlx<br/>Distance to next helix"]
        StrandDens["FEATURE_StrandDens<br/>Strand density"]
        NormDens["FEATURE_NormDens<br/>Normalized density"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Scoring Matrices"
        ScoreMxs["m_ScoreMxs[F][i][j]<br/>Feature scoring matrices"]
        Weights["m_Weights[i]<br/>Feature weights"]
        ApplyWeights["ApplyWeights()<br/>Weight application"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Position Scoring"
        GetScorePosPair["GetScorePosPair()<br/>Multi-feature position scoring"]
        FeatureSum["Sum over features<br/>Weighted combination"]
        MatchScore["Final match score<br/>Position pair score"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Alignment Scoring"
        SetSMx_NoRev["SetSMx_NoRev()<br/>Build similarity matrix"]
        SWFast["SWFast()<br/>Dynamic programming"]
        AlnFwdScore["m_AlnFwdScore<br/>Final alignment score"]
    end
    
    AA --> ScoreMxs
    NENDist --> ScoreMxs
    Conf --> ScoreMxs
    NENConf --> ScoreMxs
    RENDist --> ScoreMxs
    DstNxtHlx --> ScoreMxs
    StrandDens --> ScoreMxs
    NormDens --> ScoreMxs
    
    ScoreMxs --> ApplyWeights
    Weights --> ApplyWeights
    ApplyWeights --> GetScorePosPair
    
    GetScorePosPair --> FeatureSum
    FeatureSum --> MatchScore
    MatchScore --> SetSMx_NoRev
    SetSMx_NoRev --> SWFast
    SWFast --> AlnFwdScore
```

### Feature Scoring Implementation

The `GetScorePosPair()` method implements the multi-feature scoring:

```cpp
// For each feature in the parameter set
for (uint FeatureIdx = 0; FeatureIdx < FeatureCount; ++FeatureIdx) {
    FEATURE F = m_Params->m_Features[FeatureIdx];
    uint AlphaSize = g_AlphaSizes2[F];
    float **ScoreMx = m_Params->m_ScoreMxs[F];
    
    // Get feature values at aligned positions
    byte ia = ProfileA[FeatureIdx][PosA];
    byte ib = ProfileB[FeatureIdx][PosB];
    
    // Add weighted feature contribution
    MatchScore += ScoreMx[ia][ib];
}
```

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:320-347](), [src/dssparams.cpp:343-363](), [src/namedparams.cpp:32-53]()

## Performance Optimizations

The alignment engine implements several performance optimizations to handle large-scale protein structure searches efficiently.

### Multi-Stage Filtering Pipeline

| Stage | Method | Purpose | Threshold Parameters |
|-------|--------|---------|---------------------|
| K-mer Filter | `DoMKF()` | Skip small sequences | `m_MKFL` (sequence length) |
| Mu Filter | `MuFilter()` | Quick sequence pre-screening | `m_Omega` (score threshold) |
| Smith-Waterman | `SWFast()` | Full dynamic programming | `m_MinFwdScore` (score threshold) |
| Statistical Filter | `CalcEvalue()` | Significance testing | E-value thresholds |

### Memory Management Optimizations

- **Similarity Matrix Pooling**: `AllocSMxData()` reuses matrix memory to avoid allocation overhead [src/dssaligner.cpp:1415-1434]()
- **Dynamic Programming Row Pooling**: `AllocDProw()` reuses DP row memory [src/dssaligner.cpp:1030-1039]()
- **Profile Caching**: `SetMuQP()` pre-computes profile data for repeated use [src/dssaligner.cpp:432-454]()

### Parallel Processing Support

- **Thread-Safe Output**: `m_OutputLock` mutex protects output operations [src/dssaligner.cpp:16]()
- **Atomic Counters**: Performance statistics use atomic operations [src/dssaligner.cpp:34-40]()
- **Parasail Integration**: `m_ProfPara` enables vectorized alignment [src/dssaligner.h:37-38]()

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:705-722](), [src/dssaligner.cpp:1415-1454](), [src/dssaligner.cpp:1030-1039]()

## Statistical Significance Calculation

The alignment engine calculates statistical significance using a combination of alignment score, structural similarity (LDDT), and sequence length normalization.

### E-value Calculation Formula

The `CalcEvalue()` method implements a composite test statistic:

```cpp
const float dpw = 1.7f;      // DP score weight
const float lddtw = 0.13f;   // LDDT weight  
const float ladd = 250.0f;   // Length adjustment
const float revtsw = 2.0f;   // Reverse score weight

m_NewTestStatisticA = lddtw * LDDT;
m_NewTestStatisticA += (dpw * m_AlnFwdScore - revtsw * RevDPScore) / (L + ladd);
```

### Statistical Components

| Component | Variable | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| LDDT Score | `GetLDDT()` | Structural similarity measure |
| DP Score | `m_AlnFwdScore` | Dynamic programming alignment score |
| Reverse Score | `RevDPScore` | Self-reverse alignment normalization |
| Length Normalization | `L + ladd` | Sequence length adjustment |

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:844-898](), [src/dssaligner.cpp:1283-1294]()

# Page: DSSAligner Class

# DSSAligner Class

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/dssaligner.cpp](src/dssaligner.cpp)
- [src/dssaligner.h](src/dssaligner.h)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The `DSSAligner` class is the core alignment engine in the reseek protein structure search system. It performs pairwise sequence and structure alignments between protein chains using multiple scoring features and sophisticated filtering strategies. This class orchestrates the entire alignment workflow from input processing through statistical significance calculation to output formatting.

For information about the broader alignment pipeline and filtering systems, see [Filtering Pipeline](#4.2). For details on parameter configuration and scoring matrices, see [Parameter Configuration](#3.2).

## Class Overview

The `DSSAligner` class implements a multi-stage alignment system that combines sequence-based pre-filtering with structure-aware dynamic programming algorithms. It supports several alignment modes optimized for different speed-accuracy trade-offs and provides comprehensive statistical analysis of alignment results.

### Core Alignment Workflow

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[SetQuery] --> B[SetTarget]
    B --> C{DoMKF?}
    C -->|Yes| D[AlignMKF]
    C -->|No| E{MuFilter?}
    E -->|Pass| F[Align_NoAccel]
    E -->|Fail| G[Return]
    D --> H[PostAlignMKF]
    F --> I[CalcEvalue]
    H --> I
    I --> J[Output]
    
    F --> K[SetSMx_NoRev]
    K --> L[SWFast]
    L --> M[GetLDDT]
    M --> I
```

Sources: [src/dssaligner.h:102-231](), [src/dssaligner.cpp:783-821]()

## Key Data Members

The `DSSAligner` class maintains several categories of data members that support its alignment functionality:

### Input Data Pointers
- `m_ChainA`, `m_ChainB` - Pointers to `PDBChain` objects being aligned
- `m_ProfileA`, `m_ProfileB` - Multi-feature sequence profiles
- `m_MuLettersA`, `m_MuLettersB` - Reduced alphabet representations
- `m_MuKmersA`, `m_MuKmersB` - K-mer vectors for filtering

### Alignment Results
- `m_Path` - CIGAR-style alignment path string
- `m_LoA`, `m_LoB`, `m_HiA`, `m_HiB` - Alignment boundaries
- `m_AlnFwdScore` - Forward alignment score
- `m_Ids`, `m_Gaps` - Identity and gap counts

### Statistical Measures
- `m_EvalueA`, `m_EvalueB` - E-values for statistical significance
- `m_PvalueA`, `m_PvalueB` - P-values
- `m_QualityA`, `m_QualityB` - Quality scores
- `m_TestStatisticA`, `m_TestStatisticB` - Test statistics

Sources: [src/dssaligner.h:24-84]()

## Alignment Modes and Methods

### MKF (MuKmerFilter) Alignment

The `AlignMKF()` method implements an accelerated alignment strategy using k-mer filtering and X-drop extension:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[MuKmerFilter] --> B[FindHSPs]
    B --> C[GetMegaHSPScore]
    C --> D[XDropHSP]
    D --> E[PostAlignMKF]
```

This mode is selected when `DoMKF()` returns true, typically for longer sequences where k-mer pre-filtering provides significant speedup.

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:1358-1403]()

### Standard Smith-Waterman Alignment

The `Align_NoAccel()` method performs full Smith-Waterman alignment:

1. **Score Matrix Construction**: `SetSMx_NoRev()` builds the similarity matrix
2. **Dynamic Programming**: `SWFast()` performs optimized Smith-Waterman
3. **Statistical Analysis**: `CalcEvalue()` computes significance scores

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:923-939]()

### MuFilter Pre-filtering

The `MuFilter()` method provides a fast pre-screening step:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[MuLettersA] --> B[SetMuQP]
    C[MuLettersB] --> D[AlignMuQP]
    B --> D
    D --> E{Score >= Omega?}
    E -->|Yes| F[Continue]
    E -->|No| G[Discard]
```

This filtering uses a reduced alphabet alignment to quickly eliminate unlikely alignment pairs.

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:609-620]()

## Scoring System Integration

The `DSSAligner` integrates with the broader scoring system through several key methods:

### Multi-Feature Scoring

The `GetScorePosPair()` method computes position-specific scores across multiple features:

| Feature Type | Score Matrix | Purpose |
|-------------|-------------|---------|
| Amino Acid | `m_ScoreMxs[F]` | Sequence similarity |
| Secondary Structure | Feature-specific | Structural compatibility |
| Solvent Accessibility | Feature-specific | Surface properties |
| Other Features | Configurable | Extensible scoring |

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:320-347]()

### Gap Penalty System

Gap penalties are applied consistently across alignment modes:
- `m_GapOpen` - Gap opening penalty
- `m_GapExt` - Gap extension penalty
- Applied in `GetDPScorePath()` and related methods

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:247-318]()

## Statistical Analysis

### E-value Calculation

The `CalcEvalue()` method implements sophisticated statistical analysis:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[AlnFwdScore] --> B[GetLDDT]
    B --> C[SelfRevScore]
    C --> D[NewTestStatistic]
    D --> E[StatSig::GetEvalue]
    E --> F[Final E-value]
```

The calculation incorporates:
- **LDDT scoring** for structural similarity
- **Self-reverse scores** for normalization
- **Length normalization** factors
- **Database size** for significance testing

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:844-898]()

### LDDT Integration

The `GetLDDT()` method provides structural quality assessment by extracting aligned positions and computing Local Distance Difference Test scores.

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:1283-1294]()

## Output Generation

The `DSSAligner` supports multiple output formats through specialized methods:

### TSV Output
`ToTsv()` generates tabular output with configurable columns through the `UserField` system.

### FASTA Alignment Output
`ToFasta2()` produces aligned sequences in FASTA format with embedded statistics.

### Pretty Alignment Output
`ToAln()` creates human-readable alignment displays with scoring information.

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:1010-1028](), [src/dssaligner.cpp:975-1008](), [src/dssaligner.cpp:959-973]()

## Memory Management

The class implements custom memory management for large scoring matrices:

- `AllocSMxData()` - Allocates 2D scoring matrix with overflow protection
- `FreeSMxData()` - Deallocates matrix memory
- `m_SMx_Buffer` - Contiguous memory buffer for cache efficiency

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:1415-1454]()

## Thread Safety and Statistics

The class maintains thread-safe global statistics through atomic counters:

- `m_AlnCount` - Total alignments performed
- `m_MuFilterDiscardCount` - Alignments filtered out
- `m_XDropAlnCount` - X-drop alignments performed
- Static mutex `m_OutputLock` for thread-safe output

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:34-41](), [src/dssaligner.h:86-96]()

## Integration with Parameter System

The `DSSAligner` receives its configuration through the `DSSParams` class via `SetParams()`. This includes:
- Scoring matrices and feature weights
- Gap penalties and thresholds
- Algorithm selection flags
- Output formatting options

Sources: [src/dssaligner.cpp:648-652]()

# Parameter Configuration

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

This document covers the parameter configuration system in reseek, specifically the `DSSParams` class and its role in controlling the behavior of the core alignment engine. The parameter system provides three algorithm modes with different speed-accuracy tradeoffs, configurable feature weights, gap penalties, and filtering thresholds.

For information about the alignment algorithms themselves, see [DSSAligner Class](#3.1). For command-line options and usage, see [Commands and Options](#6.1).

## DSSParams Class Overview

The `DSSParams` class serves as the central configuration hub for the alignment engine. It manages algorithm mode selection, feature weights, scoring matrices, gap penalties, and various filtering parameters that control the speed-accuracy tradeoff of the search process.


## Algorithm Modes

The system provides three predefined algorithm modes that balance speed and sensitivity by adjusting filtering parameters:

| Mode | Speed | Sensitivity | Omega | OmegaFwd | MKFL | Use Case |
|------|-------|-------------|-------|----------|------|----------|
| **Fast** | Highest | Lowest | 22 | 50 | 500 | Large-scale screening |
| **Sensitive** | Medium | Medium | 12 | 20 | 600 | Balanced searches |
| **VerySensitive** | Lowest | Highest | 0 | 0 | 99999 | Exhaustive searches |

```mermaid

    end
    
    subgraph "Decision Modes"
        AlwaysFast["DM_AlwaysFast<br/>Force fast mode"]
        AlwaysSens["DM_AlwaysSensitive<br/>Force sensitive mode"]
        AlwaysVery["DM_AlwaysVerysensitive<br/>Force very sensitive mode"]
        UseCmdLine["DM_UseCommandLineOption<br/>Require explicit flag"]
        DefaultFast["DM_DefaultFast<br/>Default to fast if no flag"]
        DefaultSens["DM_DefaultSensitive<br/>Default to sensitive if no flag"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parameter Values"
        FastParams["Fast Mode<br/>Omega=22, MKFL=500<br/>MinHSPScore=50"]
        SensParams["Sensitive Mode<br/>Omega=12, MKFL=600<br/>MinHSPScore=50"]
        VeryParams["VerySensitive Mode<br/>Omega=0, MKFL=99999<br/>MinHSPScore=0"]
    end
    
    DecideMode --> AlwaysFast
    DecideMode --> AlwaysSens
```

| `FEATURE_NENDist` | 0.129367 | N-terminus to C-terminus distance |
| `FEATURE_Conf` | 0.202354 | Conformational similarity |
| `FEATURE_NENConf` | 0.149383 | N-terminus to C-terminus conformational similarity |
| `FEATURE_RENDist` | 0.0937677 | Relative distance features |
| `FEATURE_DstNxtHlx` | 0.00475462 | Distance to next helix |
| `FEATURE_StrandDens` | 0.0183853 | Beta strand density |
| `FEATURE_NormDens` | 0.00384384 | Normalized density |

## Parameter Validation

The system includes validation for critical parameters:

### Gap Penalty Validation

Gap penalties must be non-positive values (represented as negative numbers internally):

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Parameter Validation"
        Input["Command Line Input<br/>Positive values"]
        Convert["Internal Conversion<br/>Multiply by -1"]
        Validate["Validation Check<br/>Must be <= 0"]
        Error["Die() on Invalid<br/>Error message"]
    end
    
    Input --> Convert
    Convert --> Validate
    Validate --> Error
```

The validation ensures that gap opening and extension penalties are properly specified as non-negative values on the command line but stored as negative values internally for the alignment algorithm.

Sources: [src/dssparams.cpp:105-108]()

# Page: Database Search System

# Database Search System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/dbsearcher.cpp](src/dbsearcher.cpp)
- [src/dbsearcher.h](src/dbsearcher.h)

- [src/profileloader.cpp](src/profileloader.cpp)
- [src/profileloader.h](src/profileloader.h)
- [src/runquery.cpp](src/runquery.cpp)
- [src/search.cpp](src/search.cpp)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The Database Search System is the core component responsible for performing protein structure searches against databases of protein chains. It orchestrates multi-threaded database loading, query processing, and filtering operations to efficiently find structurally similar proteins. This system handles both query-versus-database searches and self-searches (all-versus-all comparisons within a single database).

For information about the underlying alignment algorithms, see [Core Alignment Engine](#3). For details about data format handling, see [Data Processing and Formats](#5).

## Architecture Overview

The Database Search System employs a multi-stage architecture designed for scalability and performance:

```mermaid

    subgraph "Command Interface"
        CMD["cmd_search()"]
        SELF["SelfSearch()"]
        NOFILTER["Search_NoMuFilter()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Database Search Orchestrator"
        DBS["DBSearcher"]
        SETUP["Setup()"]
        LOADDB["LoadDB()"]
        RUNQUERY["RunQuery()"]
        RUNSELF["RunSelf()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Profile Loading System"
        PL["ProfileLoader"]
        PLTHREAD["ThreadBody()"]
        PLLOAD["Load()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Filtering Pipeline"
        MUFILTER["MuPreFilter()"]
        POSTMU["PostMuFilter()"]
        REJECT["Reject()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Multi-Threading"
        QTHREAD["ThreadBodyQuery()"]
```

## Core Components

### DBSearcher Class

The `DBSearcher` class serves as the primary orchestrator for database search operations:

| Component | Purpose | Key Methods |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| Database Management | Loads and manages database chains | `LoadDB()`, `GetDBChainCount()` |
| Threading Control | Manages multi-threaded execution | `ThreadBodyQuery()`, `ThreadBodySelf()` |
| Search Orchestration | Coordinates query and self-search modes | `RunQuery()`, `RunSelf()` |
| Result Filtering | Applies E-value and statistical filters | `Reject()`, `BaseOnAln()` |

## Multi-Threading Model

The system employs a sophisticated multi-threading approach across multiple components:

### Thread Distribution

| Component | Thread Function | Purpose |
|-----------|----------------|---------|
| ProfileLoader | `StaticThreadBody()` | Load chain profiles in parallel |
| DBSearcher Query | `ThreadBodyQuery()` | Process query chains against DB |
| DBSearcher Self | `ThreadBodySelf()` | Process chain pairs in self-search |
| PostMuFilter | `ThreadBody_IndexQuery()` | Index queries for post-filtering |
| PostMuFilter | `ThreadBody_Scan()` | Scan filtered pairs |

### Thread Synchronization

# Page: DBSearcher and ProfileLoader

# DBSearcher and ProfileLoader

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/dbsearcher.cpp](src/dbsearcher.cpp)
- [src/dbsearcher.h](src/dbsearcher.h)
- [src/profileloader.cpp](src/profileloader.cpp)
- [src/profileloader.h](src/profileloader.h)
- [src/runquery.cpp](src/runquery.cpp)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The `DBSearcher` and `ProfileLoader` classes form the core database search system in reseek, responsible for loading protein structure databases and executing multi-threaded searches against them. `DBSearcher` orchestrates the entire search process, while `ProfileLoader` handles the multi-threaded loading of database chains and their derived profiles.

For information about the core alignment algorithms used by these classes, see [DSSAligner Class](#3.1). For details about the filtering pipeline that works with the search system, see [Filtering Pipeline](#4.2).

## Architecture Overview

The database search system operates as a two-phase process: database loading followed by query execution. The `ProfileLoader` handles the computationally intensive task of converting raw protein chains into searchable profiles, while `DBSearcher` manages the search execution across multiple threads.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Database Loading Phase"
        CR["ChainReader2<br/>Input Stream"]
        PL["ProfileLoader<br/>Multi-threaded Loading"]
        DSS["DSS<br/>Profile Generation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Database Storage"
        DBChains["m_DBChains<br/>vector<PDBChain*>"]
        DBProfiles["m_DBProfiles<br/>vector<vector<vector<byte>>>"]
        DBMuLetters["m_DBMuLettersVec<br/>vector<vector<byte>*>"]
        DBMuKmers["m_DBMuKmersVec<br/>vector<vector<uint>*>"]
        SelfRevScores["m_DBSelfRevScores<br/>vector<float>"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Query Execution Phase"
        QCR["ChainReader2<br/>Query Stream"]
        DBS["DBSearcher<br/>Search Orchestrator"]
        ThreadPool["Thread Pool<br/>m_DAs vector<DSSAligner*>"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Results"
        TSV["TSV Output<br/>g_fTsv"]
        ALN["Alignment Output<br/>g_fAln"]
        FASTA["FASTA Output<br/>g_fFasta2"]
    end
    
    CR --> PL
    PL --> DSS
    DSS --> DBChains
    DSS --> DBProfiles
    DSS --> DBMuLetters
    DSS --> DBMuKmers
    DSS --> SelfRevScores
    
    QCR --> DBS
    DBS --> ThreadPool
    ThreadPool --> DBChains
    ThreadPool --> DBProfiles
    ThreadPool --> DBMuLetters
    ThreadPool --> DBMuKmers
    ThreadPool --> SelfRevScores
    
    ThreadPool --> TSV
    ThreadPool --> ALN
    ThreadPool --> FASTA
```

**Database Loading and Search Architecture**

Sources: [src/dbsearcher.h:1-110](), [src/dbsearcher.cpp:242-256](), [src/profileloader.h:1-38](), [src/profileloader.cpp:73-111]()

## DBSearcher Class Structure

The `DBSearcher` class serves as the primary coordinator for database searches, managing both the database loading process and query execution phases.

### Core Data Members

| Member | Type | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| `m_Params` | `const DSSParams*` | Algorithm configuration parameters |
| `m_ThreadCount` | `uint` | Number of worker threads |
| `m_DAs` | `vector<DSSAligner*>` | Per-thread alignment engines |
| `m_DBChains` | `vector<PDBChain*>` | Database protein chains |
| `m_DBProfiles` | `vector<vector<vector<byte>>*>` | Pre-computed profiles |
| `m_DBMuLettersVec` | `vector<vector<byte>*>` | Reduced alphabet representations |
| `m_DBMuKmersVec` | `vector<vector<uint>*>` | K-mer indices for filtering |
| `m_Lock` | `mutex` | Thread synchronization |

### Key Methods

The `DBSearcher` class provides several key methods for database operations:

- `LoadDB(const string &DBFN)` - Loads database using `ProfileLoader`
- `RunQuery(ChainReader2 &QCR)` - Executes query search with threading
- `RunSelf()` - Performs all-vs-all database comparison
- `Setup()` - Initializes thread pool and alignment engines
- `ThreadBodyQuery(uint ThreadIndex, ChainReader2 *ptrQueryCR)` - Worker thread implementation

Sources: [src/dbsearcher.h:14-109](), [src/dbsearcher.cpp:73-115]()

### Threading Model

The `DBSearcher` implements a multi-threaded architecture where each thread maintains its own `DSSAligner` instance and memory pool:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Main Thread"
        Setup["Setup()<br/>Thread Initialization"]
        RunQuery["RunQuery()<br/>Search Coordination"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Thread Pool"
        T1["Thread 1<br/>m_DAs[0]"]
        T2["Thread 2<br/>m_DAs[1]"]
        TN["Thread N<br/>m_DAs[N-1]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Per-Thread Resources"
        DA1["DSSAligner<br/>Alignment Engine"]
        Mem1["XDPMem<br/>Memory Pool"]
        DA2["DSSAligner<br/>Alignment Engine"]
        Mem2["XDPMem<br/>Memory Pool"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Shared Database"
        SharedDB["m_DBChains<br/>m_DBProfiles<br/>m_DBMuLettersVec<br/>Read-Only Access"]
    end
    
    Setup --> RunQuery
    RunQuery --> T1
    RunQuery --> T2
    RunQuery --> TN
    
    T1 --> DA1
    T1 --> Mem1
    T2 --> DA2
    T2 --> Mem2
    
    T1 --> SharedDB
    T2 --> SharedDB
    TN --> SharedDB
```

**Multi-threaded Search Architecture**

Sources: [src/dbsearcher.cpp:98-106](), [src/runquery.cpp:82-125]()

## ProfileLoader Class Structure

The `ProfileLoader` class handles the multi-threaded conversion of raw protein chains into searchable profiles and derived data structures.

### Core Functionality

The `ProfileLoader::Load()` method coordinates the loading process:

```cpp
void Load(
  const DSSParams &Params,
  ChainReader2 &CR,
  vector<PDBChain *> *Chains,
  vector<vector<vector<byte> > *> *Profiles,
  vector<vector<byte> *> *MuLetters,
  vector<vector<uint> *> *KmersVec,
  vector<float> *SelfRevScores,
  uint ThreadCount)
```

### Thread Body Implementation

Each worker thread in `ProfileLoader` performs the following operations:

1. **Chain Reading**: Retrieves next chain from `ChainReader2`
2. **Profile Generation**: Creates statistical profiles using `DSS`
3. **MuLetters Generation**: Computes reduced alphabet representation
4. **MuKmers Generation**: Generates k-mer indices for filtering
5. **Self-Reverse Score**: Calculates self-alignment score for normalization

Sources: [src/profileloader.cpp:17-71](), [src/profileloader.h:24-32]()

### Data Flow Pipeline

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input"
        CR["ChainReader2<br/>Sequential Chain Access"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Thread Processing"
        GetNext["GetNext()<br/>Thread-Safe Chain Retrieval"]
        DSS["DSS.Init()<br/>Profile Generation"]
        Profile["GetProfile()<br/>Statistical Profile"]
        MuLetters["GetMuLetters()<br/>Reduced Alphabet"]
        MuKmers["GetMuKmers()<br/>K-mer Indices"]
        SelfRev["GetSelfRevScore()<br/>Self-Alignment Score"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Collections"
        Chains["m_Chains<br/>Thread-Safe Append"]
        Profiles["m_Profiles<br/>Thread-Safe Append"]
        Letters["m_MuLetters<br/>Thread-Safe Append"]
        Kmers["m_KmersVec<br/>Thread-Safe Append"]
        Scores["m_SelfRevScores<br/>Thread-Safe Append"]
    end
    
    CR --> GetNext
    GetNext --> DSS
    DSS --> Profile
    DSS --> MuLetters
    DSS --> MuKmers
    DSS --> SelfRev
    
    Profile --> Profiles
    MuLetters --> Letters
    MuKmers --> Kmers
    SelfRev --> Scores
    GetNext --> Chains
```

**ProfileLoader Processing Pipeline**

Sources: [src/profileloader.cpp:30-70]()

## Query Execution Process

The query execution process in `DBSearcher` follows a systematic approach where query chains are processed against the entire database:

### Query Thread Implementation

Each query thread processes chains sequentially:

1. **Query Setup**: Load and process query chain using `DSS`
2. **Database Iteration**: Compare against all database chains
3. **Alignment**: Use `DSSAligner` for pairwise comparison
4. **Result Output**: Generate results if alignment passes thresholds

### Performance Tracking

The `DBSearcher` maintains comprehensive performance statistics:

| Metric | Member | Purpose |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `m_ProcessedQueryCount` | `atomic<uint>` | Total queries processed |
| `m_ProcessedPairCount` | `atomic<uint>` | Total pairwise comparisons |
| `m_HitCount` | `atomic<uint>` | Alignments passing thresholds |
| `m_QPCacheHits` | `atomic<uint>` | Query-profile cache hits |
| `m_QPCacheMisses` | `atomic<uint>` | Query-profile cache misses |

Sources: [src/runquery.cpp:18-80](), [src/dbsearcher.cpp:29-56]()

## Statistical Calibration Support

The `DBSearcher` supports two types of statistical calibration for accurate E-value computation:

### Slope Calibration
When `SLOPE_CALIB` is enabled, the system loads calibrated slopes for each database chain:
- `m_ms` and `m_bs` vectors store slope parameters
- `LoadCalibratedSlopes()` reads calibration data from file
- Used for computing: `PredMinusLogP = m*TS + b`

### Gumbel Calibration
When `GUMBEL_CALIB` is enabled, the system loads Gumbel distribution parameters:
- `m_Gumbel_mus` and `m_Gumbel_betas` vectors store parameters
- `LoadGumbelCalib()` reads calibration data from file
- Used for statistical significance assessment

Sources: [src/dbsearcher.cpp:117-240]()

# Page: Filtering Pipeline

# Filtering Pipeline

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/mufilter.cpp](src/mufilter.cpp)
- [src/mukmerfilter.cpp](src/mukmerfilter.cpp)
- [src/mukmerfilter.h](src/mukmerfilter.h)
- [src/mukmerfilter2.cpp](src/mukmerfilter2.cpp)
- [src/postmufilter.cpp](src/postmufilter.cpp)
- [src/search.cpp](src/search.cpp)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The filtering pipeline implements a two-stage pre-filtering system designed to efficiently reduce the search space before performing expensive structural alignments. This system balances speed and sensitivity by using fast k-mer matching followed by detailed alignment of promising candidates.

For information about the core alignment algorithms that process the filtered results, see [Core Alignment Engine](#3). For database search orchestration and threading models, see [DBSearcher and ProfileLoader](#4.1).

## Architecture Overview

The filtering pipeline consists of two main stages that work together to identify promising alignment candidates:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Stage 1: Fast K-mer Pre-filtering"
        A[MuSeqSource] --> B[MuKmerFilter]
        B --> C[Hash Table Lookup]
        C --> D[X-drop Extension]
        D --> E[HSP Chaining]
        E --> F[Filter Results TSV]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Detailed Alignment"
        F --> G[PostMuFilter]
        G --> H[Multi-threaded Query Indexing]
        H --> I[DSSAligner]
        I --> J[Statistical Scoring]
        J --> K[Final Results]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input Data"
        L[Query Chains] --> A
        M[Database Chains] --> A
        N[MuLetters] --> B
        O[MuKmers] --> B
    end
    
    subgraph "Configuration"
        P[DSSParams] --> B
        P --> G
        Q[E-value Thresholds] --> J
        R[Threading Parameters] --> H
    end
    
    L --> H
    M --> I
```

**Two-Stage Filtering Architecture**

Sources: [src/search.cpp:64-115](), [src/postmufilter.cpp:195-284](), [src/mukmerfilter.cpp:314-387]()

## Stage 1: MuKmerFilter

The first stage performs rapid k-mer based screening using hash tables and X-drop extension algorithms.

### Core Components

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "MuKmerFilter Class"
        A[m_ptrKmerHashTableQ] --> B[Hash Table Lookup]
        C[m_ptrMuLettersQ] --> D[X-drop Extension]
        E[m_ptrMuKmersQ] --> B
        F[m_DictSize] --> B
        G[Chainer] --> H[HSP Chaining]
    end
    
    subgraph "Key Methods"
        I[SetQ] --> J[SetHashTable]
        K[GetMaxHSPScore] --> L[MuXDrop]
        M[Align] --> N[ChainHSPs]
        O[AlignBag] --> K
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Structures"
        P[m_MuKmerHSPLois] --> Q[HSP Coordinates]
        R[m_MuKmerHSPScores] --> S[HSP Scores]
        T[m_ChainHSPLois] --> U[Chained HSPs]
    end
    
    J --> B
    L --> H
    N --> U
```

**MuKmerFilter Internal Architecture**

The `MuKmerFilter` class implements the core k-mer matching algorithm:

| Component | Type | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `m_ptrKmerHashTableQ` | `uint16_t*` | Hash table for query k-mers |
| `m_DictSize` | `uint` | Size of k-mer dictionary (36^k) |
| `m_ptrMuLettersQ` | `vector<byte>*` | Query sequence in reduced alphabet |
| `m_ptrMuKmersQ` | `vector<uint>*` | Query k-mers |
| `m_C` | `Chainer` | Chains HSPs into longer alignments |

Sources: [src/mukmerfilter.h:9-97](), [src/mukmerfilter.cpp:96-102]()

### X-drop Extension Algorithm

The `MuXDrop` method implements bidirectional X-drop extension from k-mer seeds:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[K-mer Match] --> B[Forward Extension]
    A --> C[Reverse Extension]
    B --> D[Score Tracking]
    C --> E[Score Tracking]
    D --> F[X-drop Termination]
    E --> G[X-drop Termination]
    F --> H[Best Forward Score]
    G --> I[Best Reverse Score]
    H --> J[Combined HSP Score]
    I --> J
    J --> K[HSP Coordinates]
```

**X-drop Extension Process**

The algorithm extends matches in both directions until the score drops more than X below the best score seen so far. This efficiently identifies high-scoring local alignments without exhaustive dynamic programming.

Sources: [src/mukmerfilter.cpp:104-174]()

## Stage 2: PostMuFilter

The second stage performs detailed structural alignment on candidates identified by the first stage.

### Threading Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Multi-threaded Processing"
        A[LineReader2] --> B[s_ScanLock]
        B --> C[ThreadBody_Scan]
        C --> D[BCAData]
        D --> E[DSSAligner]
        E --> F[Statistical Scoring]
        F --> G[Output Files]
    end
    
    subgraph "Query Indexing"
        H[s_IndexQueryLock] --> I[ThreadBody_IndexQuery]
        I --> J[DSS Profile Generation]
        J --> K[ChainBag Creation]
        K --> L[Parasail Profiles]
    end
    
    subgraph "Synchronization"
        M[s_QueryIdx] --> N[Query Processing]
        O[s_LineIdx] --> P[Target Processing]
        Q[s_ScannedCount] --> R[Progress Tracking]
    end
    
    I --> C
    K --> E
```

**PostMuFilter Threading Model**

The `PostMuFilter` uses a two-phase threading approach:

1. **Index Phase**: Multi-threaded query indexing using `ThreadBody_IndexQuery`
2. **Scan Phase**: Multi-threaded scanning using `ThreadBody_Scan`

Sources: [src/postmufilter.cpp:36-101](), [src/postmufilter.cpp:103-192]()

### Key Data Structures

| Structure | Purpose | Thread Safety |
|-----------|---------|---------------|
| `s_ptrChainBagsQ` | Pre-computed query profiles | Protected by `s_IndexQueryLock` |
| `s_ptrLR` | Line reader for filter results | Protected by `s_ScanLock` |
| `s_fTsv` | Output file handles | Protected by `s_ScanLock` |
| `s_MaxEvalue` | E-value threshold | Read-only after initialization |

Sources: [src/postmufilter.cpp:19-34]()

## Integration with Search System

The filtering pipeline integrates with the broader search system through the `cmd_search` function:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Search Command Flow"
        A[cmd_search] --> B{optset_fast?}
        B -->|true| C[Two-stage Pipeline]
        B -->|false| D[Search_NoMuFilter]
        C --> E[MuPreFilter]
        E --> F[PostMuFilter]
        F --> G[Final Results]
        D --> G
    end
    
    subgraph "Configuration"
        H[DSSParams] --> I[DM_UseCommandLineOption]
        H --> J[DM_AlwaysSensitive]
        I --> E
        J --> F
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Flow"
        K[MuSeqSource] --> E
        L[SeqDB] --> E
        M[Filter Results TSV] --> F
        N[BCA Database] --> F
    end
```

**Search System Integration**

The pipeline is activated when the `--fast` option is specified, using different parameter sets for each stage:
- Stage 1: `DM_UseCommandLineOption` for fast filtering
- Stage 2: `DM_AlwaysSensitive` for accurate alignment

Sources: [src/search.cpp:64-115]()

## Performance Considerations

### Memory Management

The filtering pipeline uses several memory optimization strategies:

| Strategy | Implementation | Benefit |
|----------|---------------|---------|
| Hash Table Reuse | `CreateEmptyHashTable()` | Reduces allocations |
| Profile Caching | `ChainBag` structures | Avoids recomputation |
| Thread-local Storage | Per-thread `DSSAligner` | Eliminates contention |

### Statistical Tracking

The `MuKmerFilter` maintains performance statistics:

```cpp
static uint m_PairCount;
static uint m_PairWithHSPCount;
static uint m_ChainCount;
static uint m_ChainHSPCount;
```

These metrics help optimize the balance between speed and sensitivity.

Sources: [src/mukmerfilter.h:49-55](), [src/mukmerfilter.cpp:456-465]()

### Filtering Thresholds

Key parameters that control the filtering stringency:

| Parameter | Default | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `m_MKF_MinHSPScore` | 30 | Minimum HSP score to retain |
| `m_MKF_X1` | 12 | X-drop threshold |
| `s_MaxEvalue` | 10.0 | E-value cutoff for final results |
| `HASHW` | 4 | Hash table width for collision handling |

Sources: [src/mukmerfilter.cpp:337-338](), [src/postmufilter.cpp:31-32](), [src/mukmerfilter.h:7]()

# Page: Data Processing and Formats

# Data Processing and Formats

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/chainreader2.cpp](src/chainreader2.cpp)
- [src/chainreader2.h](src/chainreader2.h)
- [src/cif.cpp](src/cif.cpp)
- [src/convert.cpp](src/convert.cpp)
- [src/msta_scores.cpp](src/msta_scores.cpp)
- [src/pdbchain.cpp](src/pdbchain.cpp)
- [src/pdbchain.h](src/pdbchain.h)
- [src/seqdb.cpp](src/seqdb.cpp)
- [src/seqdb.h](src/seqdb.h)

</details>



This document covers the data processing pipeline and file format handling systems in reseek. It describes the supported input/output formats, core data structures for representing protein chains, and the unified processing architecture that converts between different structural biology file formats.

For specific details about the conversion commands and utilities, see [Format Conversion System](#5.1). For information about the internal data structures and chain management, see [Sequence and Structure Data](#5.2).

## Supported File Formats

Reseek supports multiple structural biology file formats for both input and output:

| Format | Extension | Type | Description |
|--------|-----------|------|-------------|
| PDB | `.pdb`, `.ent` | Text | Legacy Protein Data Bank format |
| CIF/mmCIF | `.cif`, `.mmcif` | Text | Modern crystallographic format |
| CAL | `.cal` | Text | C-alpha coordinate format |
| BCA | `.bca` | Binary | Binary C-alpha format |
| FASTA | `.fasta`, `.fa` | Text | Sequence-only format |

The system handles both compressed (`.gz`) and uncompressed versions of these formats automatically.

Sources: [src/chainreader2.cpp:49-87](), [src/convert.cpp:248-376]()

## Core Data Structures

### PDBChain Class

The `PDBChain` class serves as the universal internal representation for protein structures:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class PDBChain {
        +string m_Label
        +string m_Seq
        +vector~float~ m_Xs
        +vector~float~ m_Ys
        +vector~float~ m_Zs
        +vector~string~ m_Lines
        +uint m_Idx
        +GetSeqLength() uint
        +ToCal(FILE*)
        +ToFasta(FILE*)
        +ToPDB(FILE*)
        +FromPDBLines(vector~string~)
        +FromCalLines(vector~string~)
        +GetDist(uint, uint) float
        +GetXYZ(uint, float&, float&, float&)
    }
```

Key components:
- **Sequence data**: `m_Seq` stores the amino acid sequence
- **Coordinates**: `m_Xs`, `m_Ys`, `m_Zs` store C-alpha coordinates
- **Metadata**: `m_Label` for chain identification, `m_Lines` for original file content
- **Conversion methods**: `ToCal()`, `ToFasta()`, `ToPDB()` for format output

Sources: [src/pdbchain.h:10-95](), [src/pdbchain.cpp:1-498]()

### SeqDB Class

The `SeqDB` class manages collections of sequences for analysis:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class SeqDB {
        +vector~string~ m_Labels
        +vector~string~ m_Seqs
        +map~string,uint~ m_LabelToIndex
        +bool m_IsAligned
        +uint m_ColCount
        +AddSeq(string, string) uint
        +GetSeq(uint) string
        +GetLabel(uint) string
        +GetSeqByLabel(string) bool
        +FromFasta(string, bool)
        +GetSeqCount() uint
        +IsAligned() bool
    }
```

Sources: [src/seqdb.h:9-62](), [src/seqdb.cpp:9-373]()

## Processing Pipeline Architecture

The data processing pipeline follows a multi-stage architecture:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input Files<br/>(PDB, CIF, CAL, BCA, FASTA)"] --> B["PDBFileScanner"]
    B --> C["ChainReader2"]
    C --> D["Format-Specific Parsers"]
    D --> E["PDBChain Objects"]
    E --> F["Processing/Analysis"]
    F --> G["Output Writers"]
    G --> H["Output Files<br/>(Multiple Formats)"]
    
    D --> D1["GetNext_PDB()"]
    D --> D2["GetNext_CIF()"]
    D --> D3["GetNext_CAL()"]
    D --> D4["GetNext_BCA()"]
    
    G --> G1["ToCal()"]
    G --> G2["ToFasta()"]
    G --> G3["ToPDB()"]
    G --> G4["BCAData.WriteChain()"]
```

### Key Processing Components

1. **PDBFileScanner**: Discovers and queues input files
2. **ChainReader2**: Universal file reader with format detection
3. **Format-specific parsers**: Handle PDB, CIF, CAL, BCA formats
4. **PDBChain**: Universal internal representation
5. **Output writers**: Generate multiple output formats

Sources: [src/chainreader2.cpp:21-367](), [src/convert.cpp:74-246]()

## ChainReader2 State Machine

The `ChainReader2` class implements a state machine for processing different file formats:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> STATE_Closed
    STATE_Closed --> STATE_PendingFile : Open()
    STATE_PendingFile --> STATE_ReadingCALFile : .cal file
    STATE_PendingFile --> STATE_ReadingBCAFile : .bca file
    STATE_PendingFile --> STATE_ReadingPDBFile : .pdb/.ent file
    STATE_PendingFile --> STATE_ReadingCIFFile : .cif/.mmcif file
    STATE_ReadingCALFile --> STATE_PendingFile : End of file
    STATE_ReadingBCAFile --> STATE_PendingFile : End of file
    STATE_ReadingPDBFile --> STATE_PendingFile : End of file
    STATE_ReadingCIFFile --> STATE_PendingFile : End of file
    STATE_PendingFile --> STATE_Closed : No more files
```

Each state corresponds to a specific file format parser with dedicated `GetNext_*()` methods.

Sources: [src/chainreader2.h:12-21](), [src/chainreader2.cpp:116-184]()

## Multi-threaded Conversion System

The conversion system uses a thread-safe architecture for high-performance processing:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["cmd_convert()"] --> B["Thread Pool Creation"]
    B --> C["ThreadBody() instances"]
    C --> D["Shared Resources"]
    D --> E["Output Files"]
    
    D --> D1["s_fCal (CAL output)"]
    D --> D2["s_fFasta (FASTA output)"]
    D --> D3["s_fMultiPDB (PDB output)"]
    D --> D4["s_ptrBCA (BCA output)"]
    
    C --> C1["Thread 0"]
    C --> C2["Thread 1"]
    C --> C3["Thread N"]
    
    subgraph "Synchronization"
        M1["s_LockCal"]
        M2["s_LockFasta"]
        M3["s_LockMultiPDB"]
        M4["s_LockBCA"]
        M5["s_LockStats"]
    end
```

Thread safety is ensured through mutex locks for shared resources:
- `s_LockCal`: Protects CAL file writing
- `s_LockFasta`: Protects FASTA file writing  
- `s_LockMultiPDB`: Protects multi-PDB file writing
- `s_LockBCA`: Protects BCA file writing
- `s_LockStats`: Protects progress statistics

Sources: [src/convert.cpp:8-33](), [src/convert.cpp:314-325]()

## Format-Specific Processing

### PDB Format Processing

PDB files are processed using `GetFieldsFromATOMLine()` to extract:
- Atom coordinates from columns 31-54
- Amino acid type from columns 18-20
- Chain identifier from column 22
- Atom name filtering (CA atoms only)

Sources: [src/pdbchain.cpp:231-263]()

### CIF Format Processing

CIF/mmCIF files use a tabular parser that:
1. Identifies `loop_` sections with `_atom_site.*` fields
2. Maps field names to column indices
3. Extracts data from ATOM records
4. Handles model numbers and chain identifiers

Sources: [src/cif.cpp:133-309]()

### CAL Format Processing

CAL format uses a simple tab-delimited structure:
```
>chain_label
AA    X_coord    Y_coord    Z_coord
M     43.619     -1.924     8.869
N     40.445     -0.876     10.670
```

Sources: [src/chainreader2.cpp:224-288]()

### BCA Format Processing

BCA format provides binary storage for efficient access:
- Uses `BCAData` class for reading/writing
- Supports random access by chain index
- Compressed coordinate representation

Sources: [src/chainreader2.cpp:204-222]()

## Output Generation

The system supports multiple output formats simultaneously:

| Output Type | Implementation | Thread Safety |
|-------------|----------------|---------------|
| CAL | `PDBChain::ToCal()` | `s_LockCal` |
| FASTA | `PDBChain::ToFasta()` | `s_LockFasta` |
| Multi-PDB | `PDBChain::ToPDB()` | `s_LockMultiPDB` |
| BCA | `BCAData::WriteChain()` | `s_LockBCA` |
| Feature FASTA | DSS feature extraction | `s_LockFasta` |

Sources: [src/convert.cpp:157-238](), [src/pdbchain.cpp:152-188]()

# Page: Format Conversion System

# Format Conversion System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/chainreader2.cpp](src/chainreader2.cpp)
- [src/chainreader2.h](src/chainreader2.h)
- [src/cif.cpp](src/cif.cpp)
- [src/convert.cpp](src/convert.cpp)
- [src/pdbchain.cpp](src/pdbchain.cpp)
- [src/pdbchain.h](src/pdbchain.h)

</details>



The Format Conversion System provides comprehensive conversion capabilities between multiple protein structure data formats. This system handles the ingestion, processing, and output of protein chain data in formats including PDB, CIF, CAL, BCA, and FASTA. It serves as the primary data preprocessing pipeline for the reseek structural search engine.

For information about the core alignment algorithms that process converted data, see [Core Alignment Engine](#3). For details about database search operations using converted formats, see [Database Search System](#4).

## System Overview

The format conversion system is implemented primarily through the `cmd_convert()` function and supporting classes. It employs a multi-threaded architecture to efficiently process large datasets while maintaining data integrity through mutex-protected operations.

## Core Architecture

### Conversion Pipeline

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Layer"
        A[PDBFileScanner] --> B[ChainReader2]
        B --> C["PDB Files"]
        B --> D["CIF Files"] 
        B --> E["CAL Files"]
        B --> F["BCA Files"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing Layer"
        G["ThreadBody()"] --> H["PDBChain Objects"]
        H --> I["Format Validation"]
        I --> J["Chain Length Filtering"]
        J --> K["Feature Extraction"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Layer"
        L["CAL Format"] --> M["ToCal()"]
        N["FASTA Format"] --> O["ToFasta()"]
        P["BCA Format"] --> Q["BCAData::WriteChain()"]
        R["PDB Format"] --> S["ToPDB()"]
        T["Feature FASTA"] --> U["DSS Feature Extraction"]
    end
    
    A --> G
    K --> L
    K --> N
    K --> P
    K --> R
    K --> T
```

The conversion pipeline processes input files through a state machine implemented in `ChainReader2`, converts them to `PDBChain` objects, and outputs them in the requested formats.

Sources: [src/convert.cpp:248-376](), [src/chainreader2.cpp:90-184]()

### Threading Model

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Main Thread"
        A["cmd_convert()"] --> B["ThreadCount = GetRequestedThreadCount()"]
        B --> C["Create Worker Threads"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Worker Threads"
        D["ThreadBody(ThreadIndex)"] --> E["ChainReader2::GetNext()"]
        E --> F["Process PDBChain"]
        F --> G["Mutex-Protected Output"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Shared Resources"
        H["PDBFileScanner"] --> I["s_ptrFS"]
        J["Output Files"] --> K["s_fCal, s_fFasta, s_fMultiPDB"]
        L["Statistics"] --> M["s_Converted, s_TooShort, s_InputCount"]
    end
    
    C --> D
    D --> H
    G --> J
    G --> L
    
    subgraph "Synchronization"
        N["s_LockStats"] --> O["Statistics Updates"]
        P["s_LockCal"] --> Q["CAL Output"]
        R["s_LockFasta"] --> S["FASTA Output"]
        T["s_LockBCA"] --> U["BCA Output"]
    end
    
    G --> N
    G --> P
    G --> R
    G --> T
```

The system uses multiple worker threads that share a common file scanner and synchronize access to output files and statistics through dedicated mutexes.

Sources: [src/convert.cpp:74-246](), [src/convert.cpp:315-325]()

## Format Support Matrix

| Input Format | Extension | Reader Method | Output Formats |
|--------------|-----------|---------------|----------------|
| PDB | `.pdb`, `.pdb.gz`, `.ent`, `.ent.gz` | `GetFirst_PDB()` | CAL, FASTA, BCA, PDB, Feature FASTA |
| CIF/mmCIF | `.cif`, `.cif.gz`, `.mmcif`, `.mmcif.gz` | `GetFirst_CIF()` | CAL, FASTA, BCA, PDB, Feature FASTA |
| CAL | `.cal` | `GetFirst_CAL()` | CAL, FASTA, BCA, PDB, Feature FASTA |
| BCA | `.bca` | `GetFirst_BCA()` | CAL, FASTA, BCA, PDB, Feature FASTA |

Sources: [src/chainreader2.cpp:49-88]()

## Core Data Structures

### PDBChain Class

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class PDBChain {
        +string m_Label
        +string m_Seq
        +vector~float~ m_Xs
        +vector~float~ m_Ys
        +vector~float~ m_Zs
        +uint m_Idx
        +vector~string~ m_Lines
        +GetSeqLength() uint
        +FromPDBLines(Label, Lines, SaveLines) bool
        +ToCal(FILE*) void
        +ToFasta(FILE*) void
        +ToPDB(FILE*, TruncateAtZ) void
        +ToFeatureFasta(FILE*, DSS&, FEATURE) void
        +GetXYZ(Pos, x, y, z) void
        +Reverse() void
        +Flip() void
    }
    
    class ChainReader2 {
        +STATE m_State
        +PDBFileScanner* m_ptrFS
        +BCAData m_BCA
        +LineReader2 m_LR
        +Open(FileName) void
        +GetNext() PDBChain*
        +GetFirst_PDB(FN) PDBChain*
        +GetFirst_CIF(FN) PDBChain*
        +GetFirst_CAL(FN) PDBChain*
        +GetFirst_BCA(FN) PDBChain*
    }
    
    class BCAData {
        +Open(FileName) void
        +WriteChain(PDBChain&) void
        +ReadChain(Index, PDBChain&) void
        +GetChainCount() uint64
        +Close() void
    }
    
    ChainReader2 --> PDBChain : creates
    PDBChain --> BCAData : serializes to
```

The `PDBChain` class serves as the central data structure, containing both sequence information and 3D coordinates. It provides methods for conversion to all supported output formats.

Sources: [src/pdbchain.h:10-91](), [src/pdbchain.cpp:110-498]()

### State Machine Implementation

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> STATE_Closed
    STATE_Closed --> STATE_PendingFile : Open()
    STATE_PendingFile --> STATE_ReadingPDBFile : .pdb file
    STATE_PendingFile --> STATE_ReadingCIFFile : .cif file
    STATE_PendingFile --> STATE_ReadingCALFile : .cal file
    STATE_PendingFile --> STATE_ReadingBCAFile : .bca file
    STATE_ReadingPDBFile --> STATE_PendingFile : file complete
    STATE_ReadingCIFFile --> STATE_PendingFile : file complete
    STATE_ReadingCALFile --> STATE_PendingFile : file complete
    STATE_ReadingBCAFile --> STATE_PendingFile : file complete
    STATE_PendingFile --> [*] : no more files
```

The `ChainReader2` class implements a state machine that handles the sequential processing of multiple files and formats within each file.

Sources: [src/chainreader2.h:12-21](), [src/chainreader2.cpp:116-184]()

## Format-Specific Processing

### CAL Format Processing

CAL (C-Alpha List) format stores protein chains as tab-separated values with amino acid and coordinates:

```
>102l
M    43.619  -1.924  8.869
N    40.445  -0.876  10.670
I    38.254   2.240  11.220
```

The `GetNext_CAL()` method processes these files line by line, extracting amino acid sequences and 3D coordinates.

Sources: [src/chainreader2.cpp:234-288]()

### CIF Format Processing

CIF (Crystallographic Information Format) parsing involves:

1. **Parser State Machine**: `PS_WaitingForLoop` → `PS_AtLoop` → `PS_InFieldList` → `PS_InATOMs` → `PS_Finished`
2. **Field Mapping**: Dynamic field index resolution using `FieldToIdx` map
3. **Required Fields**: `_atom_site.auth_asym_id`, `_atom_site.label_atom_id`, `_atom_site.Cartn_x/y/z`

Sources: [src/cif.cpp:124-310]()

### BCA Format Processing

BCA (Binary C-Alpha) format provides efficient storage for large datasets:

- **Binary serialization** of coordinate data
- **Random access** capability through `ChainIdx_BCA`
- **Compact storage** using 16-bit integer coordinates via `CoordToIC()` conversion

Sources: [src/chainreader2.cpp:204-222](), [src/pdbchain.cpp:423-471]()

## Feature Extraction

### DSS Feature Processing

When outputting feature FASTA, the system uses the `DSS` class for structural feature extraction:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["PDBChain"] --> B["DSS::Init()"]
    B --> C["Feature Calculation"]
    C --> D["GetFeature(FEATURE, Pos)"]
    D --> E["GetFeatureChar()"]
    E --> F["Feature FASTA Output"]
    
    subgraph "Feature Types"
        G["FEATURE_SS3"]
        H["FEATURE_NENSS3"] 
        I["FEATURE_RENDist4"]
        J["FEATURE_Mu"]
    end
    
    C --> G
    C --> H
    C --> I
    C --> J
```

The `GetFeatureFromCmdLine()` function maps command-line alphabet specifications to internal feature types.

Sources: [src/convert.cpp:34-72](), [src/convert.cpp:185-203]()

## Error Handling and Statistics

The system maintains comprehensive statistics and error tracking:

- **Format Errors**: Tracked via `ChainReader2::m_CRGlobalFormatErrors`
- **Chain Filtering**: Minimum length filtering with `MinChainLength`
- **Progress Reporting**: Thread-safe progress updates with statistics
- **Label Filtering**: Optional filtering by specific chain labels

### Statistics Tracking

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Global Statistics"
        A["s_InputCount"] --> B["Total chains processed"]
        C["s_OutputCount"] --> D["Chains meeting criteria"]
        E["s_TooShort"] --> F["Chains below minimum length"]
        G["s_Converted"] --> H["Successfully converted chains"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Thread Safety"
        I["s_LockStats"] --> J["Mutex protection"]
        J --> A
        J --> C
        J --> E
        J --> G
    end
    
    subgraph "Error Tracking"
        K["ChainReader2::m_CRGlobalFormatErrors"] --> L["Format parsing errors"]
        M["Label filtering"] --> N["Missing chains report"]
    end
```

Sources: [src/convert.cpp:89-108](), [src/convert.cpp:327-368]()

## Command-Line Interface

The format conversion system integrates with the broader command-line interface supporting:

- **Input specification**: Single files or directories via `g_Arg1`
- **Output format selection**: Multiple simultaneous output formats
- **Feature extraction**: Configurable alphabet types for feature FASTA
- **Threading control**: Automatic thread count determination
- **Filtering options**: Chain length, label filtering, coordinate transformations

Key options processed by `cmd_convert()`:
- `opt(cal)`, `opt(fasta)`, `opt(bca)` - Output file specifications
- `opt(minchainlength)` - Minimum chain length filter
- `opt(alpha)` - Feature alphabet for feature FASTA
- `opt(labels)`, `opt(label)` - Chain label filtering

Sources: [src/convert.cpp:248-376]()
