## Purpose and Scope

This document covers the fundamental infrastructure components of the reseek codebase, including the application entry point, core utility functions, custom memory management system, and specialized memory classes. These components provide the foundation for all other systems in the codebase.

For information about command-line interface and option parsing, see [Commands and Options](#6.1). For build system configuration, see [Build System and CI/CD](#8.1).

## Application Entry Point

The application entry point is implemented in `reseek_main.cpp` and provides the central dispatcher for all reseek commands.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Application Lifecycle"
        A[main] --> B[MyCmdLine]
        B --> C[LogProgramInfoAndCmdLine]
        C --> D[InitTiming]
        D --> E[Command Validation]
        E --> F[Command Dispatch]
        F --> G[Memory Cleanup]
        G --> H[LogElapsedTimeAndRAM]
        H --> I[MyutilsExit]
    end
    
    subgraph "Command Processing"
        E --> J["CmdCount Check"]
        J --> K["Single Command Validation"]
        K --> L["cmd_* Function Call"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Memory Management Integration"
        B --> M["mymalloc Configuration"]
        M --> N["opt_myalloc_summary_secs"]
        M --> O["opt_myalloc_dump_secs"]
        M --> P["opt_myalloc_trace"]
        G --> Q["mymalloc_write_state"]
        G --> R["mymalloc_print_summary"]
    end
```

The main function coordinates initialization, command execution, and cleanup through these key phases:

| Phase | Function | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| Initialization | `MyCmdLine()` | Parse command line arguments |
| Logging Setup | `LogProgramInfoAndCmdLine()` | Initialize logging system |
| Timing | `InitTiming()` | Setup performance monitoring |
| Command Dispatch | Dynamic `cmd_*()` calls | Execute user-specified command |
| Cleanup | `LogElapsedTimeAndRAM()` | Report resource usage |

Sources: [src/reseek_main.cpp:10-65]()

```mermaid

```

Key file I/O functions include:

- `OpenStdioFile()` - Opens files with custom buffering
- `ReadAllStdioFile64()` - Reads entire files into memory with chunked reading for large files
- `WriteStdioFile()` - Writes data with error checking

## Memory Management System

The reseek codebase implements a custom memory management system with optional debug tracking:

### Production Memory Management

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Production Mode"
        A["myalloc"] --> B["mymalloc"]
        B --> C["malloc"]
        C --> D["User Pointer"]
        E["myfree"] --> F["free"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Debug Mode"
        G["myalloc"] --> H["mymalloc_lo"]
        H --> I["mem_data Header"]
        I --> J["malloc + metadata"]
        J --> K["InsertBlock"]
        K --> L["s_BlockList"]
        M["myfree"] --> N["DeleteBlock"]
        N --> O["Magic Check"]
        O --> P["free"]
    end
```

The system supports two compilation modes:

| Mode | Features | Performance |
|------|----------|-------------|
| Production | Direct malloc/free | High performance |
| Debug | Leak tracking, magic numbers | Development debugging |

Sources: [src/mymalloc.h:1-36](), [src/mymalloc_dbg.cpp:1-377]()

### Debug Memory Tracking

When `MYMALLOC_DBG` is enabled, the system provides comprehensive memory tracking:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Memory Block Tracking"
        A["mem_data"] --> B["magic: 0x3e3e3e3e"]
        A --> C["fn: source file"]
        A --> D["linenr: line number"]
        A --> E["bytes: allocation size"]
        A --> F["idx: allocation index"]
        A --> G["secs: timestamp"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Linked List Management"
        H["s_BlockList"] --> I["fwd pointer"]
        I --> J["bwd pointer"]
        J --> K["InsertBlock"]
        K --> L["DeleteBlock"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Reporting"
        M["mymalloc_print_summary"] --> N["Memory Statistics"]
        O["mymalloc_write_state"] --> P["Block Dump"]
        Q["mymalloc_trace"] --> R["Allocation Log"]
    end
```

Debug features include:

- **Magic Number Validation**: Detects memory corruption
- **Source Location Tracking**: Records file and line of allocation
- **Leak Detection**: Maintains active allocation list
- **Memory Maps**: Dumps process memory layout (Linux)
- **Periodic Reporting**: Automatic memory usage summaries

Sources: [src/mymalloc_dbg.cpp:12-377]()

## Specialized Memory Classes

### Matrix Template Class

The `Mx<T>` template provides efficient 2D array management:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Mx Template Structure"
        A["Mx<T>"] --> B["m_RowCount"]
        A --> C["m_ColCount"]
        A --> D["m_Data: T**"]
        A --> E["m_Buffer: T*"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Memory Layout"
        F["ONE_BUFFER Mode"] --> G["Single Allocation"]
        G --> H["Contiguous Memory"]
        H --> I["Row Pointers"]
        I --> J["Column Access"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Operations"
        K["Alloc"] --> L["FreeData"]
        L --> M["myalloc"]
        M --> N["Pointer Setup"]
        O["Get/Put"] --> P["Bounds Checking"]
    end
```

Key design features:

- **Single Buffer Mode**: Allocates contiguous memory for better cache performance
- **Type Safety**: Template-based with compile-time type checking
- **Automatic Cleanup**: RAII-style memory management
- **Bounds Checking**: Debug-mode range validation

Sources: [src/mx.h:8-138](), [src/mx.cpp:1-16]()

### XDPMem Class

The `XDPMem` class provides specialized memory management for dynamic programming algorithms:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "XDPMem Components"
        A["XDPMem"] --> B["m_LA: sequence length A"]
        A --> C["m_LB: sequence length B"]
        A --> D["m_TBBit: traceback matrix"]
        A --> E["m_RevA: reversed sequence A"]
        A --> F["m_RevB: reversed sequence B"]
        A --> G["m_Buffer1: DP row buffer"]
        A --> H["m_Buffer2: DP row buffer"]
        A --> I["m_Buffer1_Int: integer buffer"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Buffer Management"
        J["Alloc"] --> K["Clear existing"]
        K --> L["Allocate all buffers"]
        L --> M["Set dimensions"]
        N["Clear"] --> O["myfree all"]
        O --> P["Reset pointers"]
    end
```

The XDPMem class supports:

- **Sequence Alignment**: Buffers for forward and reverse sequences
- **Traceback Matrix**: 2D array for alignment path reconstruction
- **Double Buffering**: Alternating row buffers for space efficiency
- **Mixed Types**: Both float and integer buffers for different algorithms

Sources: [src/xdpmem.h:15-132]()

# Page: Advanced Algorithms and Data Structures

# Advanced Algorithms and Data Structures

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/alignpair.cpp](src/alignpair.cpp)
- [src/build_linux_x86d.bash](src/build_linux_x86d.bash)
- [src/cmd_prefiltermu.cpp](src/cmd_prefiltermu.cpp)
- [src/global.cpp](src/global.cpp)
- [src/mumx.cpp](src/mumx.cpp)
- [src/prefiltermu.cpp](src/prefiltermu.cpp)
- [src/prefiltermu.h](src/prefiltermu.h)
- [src/prefiltermuparams.h](src/prefiltermuparams.h)
- [src/prettyaln.cpp](src/prettyaln.cpp)
- [src/twohitdiag.cpp](src/twohitdiag.cpp)
- [src/twohitdiag.h](src/twohitdiag.h)
- [src/viterbifastmem.cpp](src/viterbifastmem.cpp)

</details>



This document covers the sophisticated algorithms and data structures that form the computational core of reseek's protein structure search capabilities. These include memory-efficient hash tables, k-mer based pre-filtering systems, and optimized dynamic programming implementations.

For information about the higher-level alignment engine that uses these algorithms, see [Core Alignment Engine](#3). For database search orchestration, see [Database Search System](#4).

## TwoHitDiag: Memory-Efficient Radix Hash Table

The `TwoHitDiag` class implements a specialized hash table optimized for storing sequence index and diagonal coordinate pairs during k-mer matching. This data structure is critical for the two-hit diagonal detection algorithm used in pre-filtering.

### Architecture and Memory Layout

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "TwoHitDiag Structure"
        A[m_Data] --> B["Fixed Array<br/>2M uint32_t entries<br/>16 items per radix"]
        C[m_BusyRdxs] --> D["Active Radix List<br/>16k uint32_t entries"]
        E[m_Overflows] --> F["Overflow Pointers<br/>16k uint32_t* entries"]
        G[m_Sizes] --> H["Size Tracking<br/>16k uint32_t entries"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Radix Calculation"
        I["SeqIdx, Diag"] --> J["GetRdx()"]
        J --> K["SeqIdx % 1024<br/>Diag % 16"]
        K --> L["Combined Radix<br/>14-bit index"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Item Encoding"
        M["High Bits"] --> N["SeqIdx / 1024<br/>Diag / 16"]
        N --> O["PutRaw()"]
        O --> P["32-bit Item<br/>22+10 bits"]
    end
    
    I --> J
    L --> A
    M --> A
```

The `TwoHitDiag` uses a radix-based approach where each radix can store up to 16 items in fixed memory, with overflow handling for busy radixes. The radix is calculated using the low 10 bits of the sequence index and low 4 bits of the diagonal index.

**Sources:** [src/twohitdiag.h:1-161](), [src/twohitdiag.cpp:1-661]()

### Memory Management Strategy

The data structure uses a three-tier memory management approach:

| Component | Size | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| Fixed Storage | 2M uint32_t | Primary storage for 16 items per radix |
| Busy Tracking | 64KB | Tracks which radixes contain data |
| Overflow Buffers | Variable | Dynamic allocation for busy radixes |

The `Add()` method [src/twohitdiag.cpp:47-99]() handles the complex logic of item placement, overflow detection, and memory expansion.

**Sources:** [src/twohitdiag.h:38-54](), [src/twohitdiag.cpp:29-46]()

## PrefilterMu: K-mer Based Pre-filtering Algorithm

The `PrefilterMu` class implements a sophisticated two-stage pre-filtering system using k-mer neighborhoods and two-hit diagonal detection. This algorithm significantly reduces the search space before expensive alignment computations.

### Algorithm Workflow

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Target Sequence"] --> B["Extract K-mers<br/>GetKmers()"]
    B --> C["For each k-mer<br/>Search_TargetKmerNeighborhood()"]
    C --> D["Build High-scoring<br/>Neighborhood<br/>GetHighScoringKmers()"]
    D --> E["Query Index Lookup<br/>Search_Kmer()"]
    E --> F["Diagonal Calculation<br/>getd(QPos, TPos)"]
    F --> G["Store in TwoHitDiag<br/>m_DiagBag.Add()"]
    G --> H["Find Duplicates<br/>SetDupes()"]
    H --> I["Extend to HSPs<br/>ExtendTwoHitDiagsToHSPs()"]
    I --> J["Score with FindHSP()"]
    J --> K["Ranked Results<br/>AddTwoHitDiag()"]
```

The algorithm uses a 5-mer with pattern "1110011" (7 positions, 5 used) and builds neighborhoods of high-scoring k-mers around each target k-mer.

**Sources:** [src/prefiltermu.cpp:145-151](), [src/prefiltermu.cpp:153-178]()

### K-mer Neighborhood Construction

The pre-filtering system builds high-scoring k-mer neighborhoods using the `MerMx` scoring matrix. For each target k-mer, it identifies query k-mers that score above a threshold:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Target K-mer"] --> B["MerMx.GetHighScoringKmers()"]
    B --> C["Neighborhood K-mers<br/>Score >= MIN_KMER_PAIR_SCORE"]
    C --> D["Query Index Lookup<br/>MuDex.GetRowSize()"]
    D --> E["Diagonal Matches<br/>diag.getd()"]
    E --> F["TwoHitDiag.Add()"]
```

The neighborhood construction uses a minimum k-mer pair score of 36 [src/prefiltermuparams.h:22]() to balance sensitivity and specificity.

**Sources:** [src/prefiltermu.cpp:153-178](), [src/prefiltermuparams.h:1-24]()

## Memory-Efficient Alignment Algorithms

### ViterbiFastMem: Optimized Viterbi Algorithm

The `ViterbiFastMem` function implements a memory-efficient version of the Viterbi algorithm for sequence alignment using banded dynamic programming.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Memory Management"
        A[XDPMem] --> B["GetDPRow1()<br/>M-state scores"]
        A --> C["GetDPRow2()<br/>D-state scores"]
        A --> D["GetTBBit()<br/>Traceback bits"]
    end
    
    subgraph "DP Computation"
        E["For each position (i,j)"] --> F["Compute M-state<br/>Match/Mismatch"]
        F --> G["Compute D-state<br/>Deletion"]
        G --> H["Compute I-state<br/>Insertion"]
        H --> I["Store TraceBits<br/>Optimal transition"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Traceback"
        J["Final State"] --> K["TraceBackBitMem()"]
        K --> L["Reconstruct Path<br/>M/D/I operations"]
    end
    
    A --> E
    I --> J
```

The algorithm uses rolling arrays to minimize memory usage while maintaining O(LA × LB) time complexity for sequences of length LA and LB.

**Sources:** [src/viterbifastmem.cpp:32-192]()

### Gap Penalty Handling

The Viterbi implementation supports sophisticated gap penalty schemes:

```cpp
// Terminal gap penalties (different from internal)
float s_TermOpen = 0;
float s_TermExt = 0;

// Internal gap penalties
float s_Open = -1;
float s_Ext = -0.05f;
```

Gap penalties are configurable through the `gapstr` parameter format: `open_ext_termopen_termext`.

**Sources:** [src/viterbifastmem.cpp:6-30]()

## Alignment Pair Processing

### PairAligner: Comprehensive Alignment Workflow

The `alignpair.cpp` module provides end-to-end alignment processing for protein structure pairs:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Input Chains<br/>PDB/CIF format"] --> B["ChainReader2<br/>Parse structures"]
    B --> C["DSS.Init()<br/>Generate profiles"]
    C --> D["GetSelfRevScore()<br/>Self-alignment baseline"]
    D --> E["DSSAligner.SetQuery()<br/>DSSAligner.SetTarget()"]
    E --> F["AlignQueryTarget()<br/>Core alignment"]
    F --> G["Kabsch Transform<br/>Structural superposition"]
    G --> H["Output Generation<br/>Alignment files"]
```

The alignment process includes self-reverse scoring to establish baselines and Kabsch transformation for structural superposition.

**Sources:** [src/alignpair.cpp:77-145](), [src/alignpair.cpp:147-209]()

### Pretty Alignment Formatting

The `prettyaln.cpp` module formats alignment results for human readability:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Alignment Path"] --> B["Parse Path String<br/>M/D/I operations"]
    B --> C["Calculate Statistics<br/>Identity, Gaps"]
    C --> D["Format Alignment<br/>WriteLocalAln()"]
    D --> E["Annotation Characters<br/>|, :, ., space"]
    E --> F["Summary Statistics<br/>AQ, E-value"]
```

The formatting includes BLOSUM62-based annotation characters and comprehensive alignment statistics.

**Sources:** [src/prettyaln.cpp:26-99]()

## Supporting Data Structures

### MerMx: K-mer Scoring Matrix

The `MerMx` class provides k-mer neighborhood scoring capabilities used by the pre-filtering system:

```mermaid
graph TB
    A["Substitution Matrix<br/>36x36 amino acids"] --> B["MerMx.Init()"]
    B --> C["BuildSelfScores_Kmers()<br/>Precompute k-mer scores"]
    C --> D["GetHighScoringKmers()<br/>Neighborhood construction"]
    D --> E["PrefilterMu<br/>Two-hit diagonal detection"]
```

The matrix supports a 36-letter alphabet for reduced amino acid representation used in 3Di structural alphabets.

**Sources:** [src/mumx.cpp:15-31](), [src/mumx.cpp:33-172]()

### Thread-Safe Result Collection

The pre-filtering system uses thread-safe result collection through the `RankedScoresBag` class:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Multiple Threads"] --> B["PrefilterMu.Search()"]
    B --> C["Thread-local Results"]
    C --> D["Mutex Protection<br/>m_Lock.lock()"]
    D --> E["RankedScoresBag<br/>Global result collection"]
```

This design enables parallel processing of target sequences while maintaining result integrity.

**Sources:** [src/cmd_prefiltermu.cpp:16-49](), [src/prefiltermu.cpp:344-373]()

# Page: Testing and Validation

# Testing and Validation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [test_data/dom_scopid.tsv](test_data/dom_scopid.tsv)
- [test_results/success_list.txt](test_results/success_list.txt)
- [test_scripts/check_scop40.py](test_scripts/check_scop40.py)
- [test_scripts/scop40.py](test_scripts/scop40.py)

</details>



This document covers the comprehensive testing and validation framework for the reseek protein structure search system. The testing infrastructure focuses on performance benchmarking, statistical validation, and quality assurance procedures to ensure search accuracy and reliability.

For information about the benchmarking analysis tools, see [Analysis and Benchmarking](#7). For details about the core alignment algorithms being tested, see [Core Alignment Engine](#3).

## Testing Framework Overview

The reseek testing system implements a multi-layered validation approach combining automated performance benchmarking, statistical analysis, and continuous integration testing. The framework validates search sensitivity, specificity, and computational performance across different algorithm configurations.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Test Infrastructure"
        A[check_scop40.py] --> B[scop40.py]
        C[success_list.txt] --> D["Version Tracking"]
        E["Test Scripts"] --> F["Automated Execution"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Validation Targets"
        G["Fast Mode"] --> H["Performance Metrics"]
        I["Sensitive Mode"] --> H
        J["Very Sensitive Mode"] --> H
        K["E-value Calibration"] --> H
    end
    
    subgraph "Benchmark Data"
        L["SCOP40 Database"] --> M["Gold Standard"]
        N["Domain Classifications"] --> M
        O["Test Queries"] --> M
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Validation"
        P["ROC Analysis"] --> Q["Quality Metrics"]
        R["Sensitivity Curves"] --> Q
        S["Statistical Tests"] --> Q
    end
    
    A --> G
    A --> I
    A --> J
    A --> K
    
    B --> L
    B --> N
    B --> O
    
    H --> P
    H --> R
    H --> S
    
    D --> F
    F --> A
    Q --> C
```

**Test Architecture Overview**

The testing framework operates through coordinated Python scripts that execute reseek with different parameter configurations and validate results against known benchmarks.

Sources: [test_scripts/check_scop40.py:1-55](), [test_scripts/scop40.py:1-571](), [test_results/success_list.txt:1-25]()

## SCOP40 Benchmarking System

The primary validation system uses the SCOP40 benchmark, a gold standard dataset for protein structure classification. The `Scop40` class provides comprehensive evaluation capabilities for measuring search performance across different classification levels.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "SCOP40 Evaluation Pipeline"
        A["Query Results"] --> B["scop40.py"]
        C["Domain Mapping"] --> B
        D["SCOP Classifications"] --> B
        
        B --> E["TP/FP Classification"]
        E --> F["Statistical Analysis"]
        F --> G["Performance Metrics"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Classification Levels"
        H["Family Level"] --> I["fam1"]
        J["Superfamily Level"] --> K["sf2/sf3/sf4"]
        L["Fold Level"] --> M["fold5/fold6"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Performance Measures"
        N["Sensitivity (TPR)"] --> O["SEPQ Metrics"]
        P["Specificity"] --> O
        Q["ROC Area"] --> O
        R["Precision"] --> O
    end
    
    I --> E
    K --> E
    M --> E
    
    G --> N
    G --> P
    G --> Q
    G --> R
```

**SCOP40 Benchmark Architecture**

The benchmark system evaluates protein structure search results against hierarchical SCOP classifications to measure true positive and false positive rates at different stringency levels.

### Key Validation Components

| Component | Class/Function | Purpose |
|-----------|----------------|---------|
| Benchmark Controller | `Scop40` | Main evaluation class for SCOP40 analysis |
| Classification Logic | `is_tp()` | Determines true/false positives by SCOP level |
| Performance Metrics | `eval_sorted()` | Calculates sensitivity and specificity |
| Statistical Analysis | `get_summary()` | Generates performance summary statistics |

The `Scop40` class supports multiple evaluation levels:
- **fam1**: Family-level classification (most stringent)
- **sf2/sf3/sf4**: Superfamily-level variants
- **fold5/fold6**: Fold-level classification (most permissive)

Sources: [test_scripts/scop40.py:26-427](), [test_scripts/scop40.py:176-247]()

**Performance Metrics Calculation Pipeline**

The system processes search results through statistical analysis to generate standardized performance measures for algorithm validation.

### Critical Performance Thresholds

The validation system enforces minimum performance requirements:

```python
# Expected performance thresholds from check_scop40.py
FAST_MODE_THRESHOLDS = {
    'SEPQ0.1': 0.2107,  # Sensitivity at 0.1 false positives per query
    'SEPQ1': 0.3144,    # Sensitivity at 1 false positive per query  
    'SEPQ10': 0.3882    # Sensitivity at 10 false positives per query
}
```

The test framework validates that each algorithm mode meets or exceeds these performance benchmarks, with a tolerance of -0.01 for regression detection.

Sources: [test_scripts/check_scop40.py:44-50](), [test_scripts/scop40.py:249-427]()

**Automated Test Execution and Tracking**

### Test Results Format

The `success_list.txt` file maintains a chronological record of successful test runs:

| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| Version | Software version with build hash | `reseekv2.6.i86linux64[a4334f7]` |
| Timestamp | Test execution time | `2025-07-09/08:28:10` |
| Status | Test outcome tracking | Implicit success if listed |

The system tracks 25 successful test runs spanning from version 1.0 to 2.6, demonstrating continuous validation across major releases.

Sources: [test_results/success_list.txt:1-25](), [test_scripts/check_scop40.py:10-54]()

## Statistical Validation Framework

The testing system implements comprehensive statistical analysis to ensure robust performance evaluation.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Statistical Analysis Components"
        A["eval_sorted()"] --> B["Hit Classification"]
        C["Domain Mapping"] --> B
        D["Score Sorting"] --> B
        
        B --> E["TP/FP Accumulation"]
        E --> F["TPR Calculation"]
        E --> G["FPR Calculation"]
        E --> H["Precision Calculation"]

    subgraph "Performance Curves"

        K["plot_fprs[]"] --> J
        L["plot_epqs[]"] --> J
        M["plot_scores[]"] --> J
        N["plot_precisions[]"] --> J
    end
    
    subgraph "Key Statistics"
        O["roc_area()"] --> P["AUC Calculation"]
        Q["sens_to_firstfp"] --> R["First FP Sensitivity"]
        S["tpr_at_fpepq*"] --> T["Threshold Metrics"]
    end

        U["is_tp()"] --> V["Classification Rules"]

    J --> S
    
    V --> B
    P --> T
    R --> T
```

**Statistical Validation Architecture**

The framework provides detailed statistical analysis including ROC curves, precision-recall metrics, and threshold-based performance measures.

### Classification Logic

The `is_tp()` method implements hierarchical classification rules:

- **Family Level (fam1)**: Same family = TP, different fold = FP, same fold = ignore
- **Superfamily Level (sf2)**: Same superfamily = TP, different = FP
- **Fold Level (fold5/fold6)**: Same fold = TP, different = FP

This hierarchical approach enables evaluation at multiple stringency levels, from strict family-based classification to permissive fold-based matching.

Sources: [test_scripts/scop40.py:176-247](), [test_scripts/scop40.py:249-427](), [test_scripts/scop40.py:460-468]()

## Quality Assurance Procedures

The testing framework enforces quality standards through automated validation and regression detection.

| Quality Check | Implementation | Threshold |
|---------------|---------------|-----------|
| Performance Regression | `check_scop40.py` error detection | -0.01 tolerance |
| Statistical Validation | ROC analysis and AUC calculation | Mode-specific targets |
| Data Integrity | Sort order validation | Score monotonicity |
| Version Tracking | Build hash and timestamp logging | Continuous integration |

The system automatically fails tests that fall below performance thresholds, providing immediate feedback on algorithm changes that may degrade search quality.

Sources: [test_scripts/check_scop40.py:28-54](), [test_scripts/scop40.py:301-305]()
